name: Barbell Bench Press
setup: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under a barbell on the rack, feet flat on the floor, and hands a little wider than your shoulders, ideally with a spotter behind you.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down, squeeze your glutes, then unrack the bar and hold it over your shoulders with straight arms.
Take a big breath, brace your core, and lower the bar under control to touch your mid chest, with your elbows about forty-five degrees from your body.
Press the bar up and slightly back toward your shoulders until your arms are straight, keeping your feet planted and your head on the bench.
When you finish, steer the bar back until it touches the hooks, then lower it into place and let go.
cues: Feet planted, drive through the floor
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off your chest
Lifting your hips off the bench
Flaring elbows straight out to the sides

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about thirty degrees, sit back with a dumbbell on each thigh, and kick the weights up to chest height.
steps: Plant your feet, pull your shoulder blades back and down, and hold the dumbbells over your upper chest with palms facing forward.
Lower the weights slowly until your elbows are just below the bench, with your forearms staying vertical.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly together until your arms are straight, without letting your shoulders roll forward.
mistakes: Bouncing the weights at the bottom

name: Dumbbell Flys
setup: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand, holding the weights over your chest with your palms facing each other.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down, then soften your elbows into a slight bend that you keep the same all the way through.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until your elbows are about level with the bench and you feel a chest stretch.
Squeeze your chest to sweep the dumbbells back up along the same arc, as if hugging a big tree, until they almost touch over your chest.
mistakes: Turning the fly into a press
Going too heavy to control it
Lowering far past a comfortable stretch

name: Cable Crossovers
setup: Set both pulleys of a cable station high, grab a handle in each hand, and step forward into a staggered stance, leaning slightly forward with your arms out wide.
steps: Start with your arms open wide, hands about shoulder height, elbows softly bent, chest lifted, and a gentle stretch across your chest.
Sweep your hands down and together in a wide arc until they meet in front of your lower chest, squeezing your chest hard.
Pause for one second, then slowly open your arms back out along the same arc, keeping the same elbow bend and your torso still.
cues: Squeeze your chest at the end
mistakes: Swinging your torso to finish reps
Letting the cables yank your arms back
Turning the move into a press

name: Push-Ups
setup: Hands on the floor a bit wider than your shoulders, body in one straight line, toes on the floor.
steps: Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows tucked at about forty-five degrees.
Stop an inch above the floor, then push back up to straight arms.
Keep your core tight so the hips move with the shoulders.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about thirty degrees, lie back with your eyes under a barbell on the rack, and take a grip a little wider than your shoulders.
steps: Plant your feet, pull your shoulder blades back and down, and press the bar off the hooks until it hangs over your upper chest.
Breathe in, brace your core, and lower the bar in a smooth line until it lightly touches your upper chest, just below your collarbone.
Press the bar up and slightly back until your arms are fully straight over your shoulders, keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Rack the bar by guiding it back into the hooks before you let go, and have a spotter nearby for heavy sets.
cues: Hips stay glued to the bench
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off your chest
Letting your hips lift off the bench

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
setup: Hook your feet securely under the pads of a decline bench, lie back with your eyes under a barbell on the rack, and take a grip a little wider than your shoulders.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades together, press the bar off the hooks, and hold it over your lower chest with your arms straight.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until it lightly touches your lower chest, keeping your elbows about forty-five degrees from your sides.
Press the bar up until your arms are straight, driving evenly with both hands and keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Guide the bar back into the hooks before letting go, and always use a spotter on a decline bench.
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off your chest
Letting the bar drift toward your face
Skipping the spotter on heavy sets

name: Pause Bench Press
setup: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under a barbell on the rack, feet flat on the floor, hands a little wider than your shoulders, and a spotter behind you.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down, press the bar off the hooks, and hold it over your shoulders with straight arms.
Breathe in, brace your core, and lower the bar under control until it rests lightly on your mid chest.
Hold the bar still on your chest for a full two-second count, keeping your upper back tight and your core braced.
After the pause, press the bar up hard until your arms are straight, then lower into the next rep and pause again.
mistakes: Relaxing and sinking at the bottom
Bouncing the bar off your chest
Going too heavy to hold the pause

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
setup: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh, then lie back and kick the weights up to chest height with your feet flat on the floor.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down, then press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight over your chest with your palms facing your feet.
Lower the dumbbells slowly to the sides of your mid chest until your elbows are just below the bench, keeping your forearms straight up and down.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly together until your arms are straight, then repeat. To finish, lower the weights to your thighs and sit up.
cues: Squeeze your chest at the top
mistakes: Letting the dumbbells drift out wide
Elbows flared straight out to the sides

name: Decline Dumbbell Press
setup: Hook your feet securely under the pads of a decline bench, then lie back with a dumbbell on each thigh and bring the weights up to chest height.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back, then press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight over your lower chest, with your palms facing your feet.
Lower the dumbbells slowly to the sides of your lower chest, with your elbows about forty-five degrees from your body and your forearms straight up and down.
Press the weights up and slightly together until your arms are straight. To finish the set, bring the dumbbells down to your thighs before you sit up.
mistakes: Letting the dumbbells drift out wide

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Press
setup: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and one dumbbell held over your chest in your right hand, with your other hand resting on your stomach.
steps: Squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and pull your shoulder blades back so your body stays square and does not roll sideways.
Lower the dumbbell slowly to the side of your chest until your elbow is just below the bench, keeping your forearm straight up and down.
Press the weight back up until your arm is straight over your shoulder, finish all your reps on this side, and then switch arms.
mistakes: Rolling your body toward the weight
Letting the dumbbell wobble out wide
Arching your lower back off the bench

name: Incline Dumbbell Flys
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about thirty degrees, lie back with a dumbbell in each hand, and hold the weights over your upper chest with your palms facing each other.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down, keep a soft bend in your elbows, and keep that same bend for the whole rep.
Open your arms in a wide arc until your elbows are about level with your shoulders and you feel a stretch across your upper chest.
Squeeze your chest to sweep the weights back up along the same arc, finishing with the dumbbells almost touching over your upper chest.
mistakes: Swinging the weights up with momentum

name: Low-to-High Cable Flys
setup: Set both pulleys of a cable station low, grab a handle in each hand, and step forward into a staggered stance with your torso leaning slightly forward and your elbows slightly bent.
steps: Begin with your hands low and out wide by your hips, elbows softly bent, and a gentle stretch across your chest.
Sweep your hands up and together in a scooping arc until they meet in front of your upper chest, squeezing your chest hard.
Pause for one second, then slowly lower your hands back out and down along the same arc, keeping your elbows softly bent and your torso still.
mistakes: Swinging your body to move the cables
Bending and straightening your elbows each rep

name: Pec Deck Flys
setup: Sit on a pec deck machine with your back flat against the pad, adjust the seat so the handles sit at chest height, and grip them with your elbows softly bent.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down against the pad, lift your chest, and keep your feet flat on the floor.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a smooth hugging arc, squeezing your chest for a moment when they meet.
Let the handles open back slowly until your elbows are about in line with your shoulders, without letting the weight pull your shoulders forward.
mistakes: Using momentum to swing the handles
Seat set too low or too high

name: Machine Chest Press
setup: Sit on a chest press machine, adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid chest, and hold the handles with your back flat against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down against the pad, brace your core, and keep your wrists in line with your forearms.
Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight, without letting your shoulders roll forward off the pad.
Return the handles slowly until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest, and stop before the weight stack touches down.
cues: Shoulder blades back on the pad
mistakes: Seat too low, handles below chest
Letting the weight stack slam down

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
setup: Place a flat bench inside a Smith machine so the bar lines up with your mid chest, then lie back with your feet flat on the floor and your hands a little wider than your shoulders.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down, push the bar up, and twist your hands to unhook it so the bar is over your chest.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to touch your mid chest, keeping your elbows about forty-five degrees from your sides and your wrists straight.
Press the bar straight up along its track until your arms are straight, without letting your hips lift off the bench.
When you finish, push the bar up, twist your hands back to hook it onto the rack, and only then let go.
cues: Bar lines up with mid chest
mistakes: Bench too far forward or back
Letting your hips lift off the bench

name: Cable Chest Press
setup: Set both cable pulleys to chest height, stand with your back to the machine holding a handle in each hand, and step forward into a staggered stance with your elbows bent and hands beside your chest.
steps: Brace your core, keep a slight forward lean, and pull your shoulder blades back so your chest is open and your torso stays still.
Press both handles straight forward until your arms are almost straight and your hands meet in front of your chest, squeezing your chest at the end.
Bring the handles back slowly until your hands are beside your chest and you feel a gentle stretch, keeping your stance steady.
cues: Press straight in front of you
mistakes: Leaning in to push the weight
Letting the cables pull you off balance

name: Incline Push-Ups
muscles: Lower chest, front shoulders, triceps, core
setup: Place your hands on the edge of a sturdy bench or countertop a little wider than your shoulders, and step your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so your body stays in one straight line, with your neck in line with your spine.
Lower your chest toward the bench until it is just above the edge, with your elbows angled about forty-five degrees from your sides.
Push through your palms until your arms are straight, keeping your hips from sagging or rising as you go.
mistakes: Stopping well short of the bench

name: Decline Push-Ups
muscles: Upper chest, front shoulders, triceps, core
setup: Place your feet on a sturdy bench or box, then walk your hands out onto the floor a little wider than your shoulders until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so your body stays in one straight sloping line and your hips do not sag.
Lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows angled about forty-five degrees from your sides, until you are a few inches above the floor.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight, keeping your core tight and your neck in line with your spine.
mistakes: Hips piking up toward the ceiling
Cutting the range of motion short

name: Deficit Push-Ups
setup: Place your hands on two sturdy blocks or push-up handles set a little wider than your shoulders, step your feet back, and hold a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body stays in one straight line, with your shoulders stacked over your hands.
Lower your chest slowly between your hands, past the level of the blocks, until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest.
Press back up until your arms are straight, keeping your elbows about forty-five degrees from your body and your hips from sagging.
mistakes: Sinking deeper than you can control
Using blocks that wobble or slide

name: Wide Push-Ups
setup: Start in a high plank on the floor with your hands wider than your shoulders, fingers pointing forward or slightly out, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and press your hands firmly into the floor so your shoulders feel strong and steady.
Lower your chest toward the floor, letting your elbows angle out about sixty degrees from your body, until your chest is a few inches off the floor.
Press the floor away until your arms are straight, keeping your hips in line and your neck relaxed and neutral.
cues: Hands wide, body in one line
mistakes: Hands set wider than you can control

name: Knee Push-Ups
setup: Kneel on a mat with your hands on the floor just wider than your shoulders, then walk your knees back until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
steps: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so your hips neither drop nor stick up, and look at a spot just ahead of your hands.
Lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows angled about forty-five degrees from your sides, until your chest is a few inches above the mat.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight, keeping the line from your head to your knees solid the whole time.
mistakes: Sitting your hips back toward your heels
Hips sticking up in the air
Only bending a little at the elbows

name: Archer Push-Ups
setup: Start in a high plank on the floor with your hands set much wider than your shoulders, fingers pointing slightly out, and your feet about hip width apart.
steps: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body stays in one straight line from your head to your heels.
Shift your weight toward your right hand and bend that elbow to lower your chest toward it, keeping your left arm straight.
Push through your bent arm to return to the middle, letting your straight arm help only as much as you need to.
Repeat to the left, bending your left elbow and straightening your right arm. One lower to each side is one rep.
cues: Hips stay square to the floor
mistakes: Twisting your hips toward the bent arm
Bending both elbows the same amount
Going wider than you can control

name: Clap Push-Ups
setup: Start in a high plank on a mat with your hands just wider than your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and lower your chest toward the floor under control until your elbows are bent to about ninety degrees.
Push up hard and fast through your palms so your hands leave the floor, and clap them together quickly in front of your chest.
Land softly with your hands back under your shoulders, letting your elbows bend a little to absorb the landing, and keep your body straight.
Flow straight into the next rep, and stop the set as soon as your pushes slow down or your hips start to sag.
mistakes: Pushing on after your form breaks down

name: Chest Dips
setup: Grip the parallel bars of a dip station, press up until your arms are straight, then lean your torso forward and cross your ankles behind you.
steps: Keep your chest lifted and your shoulders down away from your ears, with a slight forward lean that you hold for every rep.
Bend your elbows and lower your body slowly, letting your elbows flare slightly out, until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press through your palms to push yourself back up until your arms are straight, squeezing your chest as you rise.
mistakes: Sinking so low your shoulders strain
Staying fully upright instead of leaning

name: Svend Press
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and press a light weight plate between your palms at chest height, with your fingers pointing up and your elbows bent.
steps: Squeeze the plate hard between your palms and keep squeezing for the whole set, with your core braced and your shoulders down.
Press the plate straight out in front of your chest until your arms are almost straight, still squeezing the plate.
Pull the plate slowly back to your chest, keeping the squeeze on and the plate upright the entire time.
mistakes: Letting your grip on the plate loosen
Using a plate that is too heavy

name: Floor Press
setup: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your elbows resting on the floor and your forearms vertical.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the floor and brace your core so your lower back stays in a comfortable, natural position.
Press the dumbbells straight up over your chest until your arms are straight, with your palms facing your feet or each other.
Lower the weights slowly, with your elbows about forty-five degrees from your body, until your upper arms lightly touch the floor, then pause and press back up.
mistakes: Bouncing your arms off the floor
Relaxing your shoulders at the bottom
Flaring elbows wide away from your body

name: Dumbbell Pullovers
setup: Lie back on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and hold one dumbbell upright above your chest, with both hands cupped under the top plate.
steps: Brace your core, keep a slight bend in your elbows, and keep your ribs down so your lower back does not arch up off the bench.
Breathe in and slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc back over your head, stopping where you feel a stretch before your lower back starts to arch.
Breathe out and pull the dumbbell back up along the same arc until it is over your chest, squeezing your chest and the sides of your back.
mistakes: Arching your lower back off the bench
Turning it into a triceps extension
Using a weight that is too heavy

name: Band Chest Press
setup: Wrap a resistance band around a sturdy post behind you at chest height, hold one end in each hand, and stand in a staggered stance with your hands beside your chest.
steps: Brace your core, lean slightly forward, and pull your shoulder blades back so there is tension on the band before you start.
Press both hands straight forward until your arms are almost straight, keeping your wrists strong and your hands at chest height.
Bring your hands back slowly to your chest, fighting the band the whole way instead of letting it snap you back.
mistakes: Letting the band snap your hands back
Anchor point set too high or low

name: Band Chest Flys
setup: Anchor a resistance band behind you at chest height, hold one end in each hand, and stand in a staggered stance with your arms out to the sides and your elbows softly bent.
steps: Lean slightly forward, brace your core, and let your arms open wide with a soft bend in your elbows until you feel a gentle stretch.
Sweep your hands together in a wide arc until they meet in front of your chest, and squeeze your chest for a second.
Open your arms slowly back out along the same arc, keeping your elbow bend the same and your torso still.
mistakes: Bending your elbows into a press
Rushing back out with the band

name: Barbell Overhead Press
muscles: Front and side shoulders, triceps, upper traps, core
setup: Set a barbell in a rack at upper chest height, grip it just outside shoulder-width with your palms facing forward, then lift it off and step back with your feet hip-width apart.
steps: Rest the bar on your front shoulders with your elbows just ahead of it, squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and pull your ribs down.
Press the bar straight up, tucking your chin back slightly so it clears your face, then push your head forward once the bar passes.
Lock out with the bar over the middle of your feet, your biceps by your ears, and your ribs still pulled down.
Lower the bar under control back to your front shoulders, then take a fresh breath and brace again before the next rep.
mistakes: Leaning back and arching your lower back
Pressing the bar out in front of you
Flaring your ribs open at the top

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
muscles: Front and side shoulders, triceps, upper traps
setup: Sit on a bench with an upright back pad and your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell at each shoulder with your palms facing forward.
steps: Press your back against the pad, brace your core, and pull your ribs down so your lower back does not arch.
Press both dumbbells up until your arms are straight and the weights are directly over your shoulders.
Pause for a moment without shrugging, then lower the weights slowly to shoulder height with your forearms staying vertical.
cues: Ribs down, back on the pad
mistakes: Arching your lower back off the pad
Letting your elbows drift behind your body
Dropping the weights down too fast

name: Lateral Raises
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing in and a small bend in your elbows.
steps: Brace your core, pull your ribs down, and let your shoulders relax away from your ears.
Raise both arms out to your sides in a wide arc, leading with your elbows, until your hands reach about shoulder height.
Pause for a moment, then lower the dumbbells slowly over about three seconds without letting them swing.
mistakes: Swinging the weights up with momentum
Shrugging your shoulders toward your ears
Raising your arms above shoulder height

name: Bent-Over Rear Delt Flys
muscles: Rear shoulders, upper back, mid traps
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart holding a light dumbbell in each hand, push your hips back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, and let your arms hang below your chest.
steps: Soften your knees, keep your back flat from your head to your hips, brace your core, and look at the floor just ahead of your feet.
With a small bend in your elbows, raise both arms out to the sides in a wide arc until your hands are level with your back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades gently at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly without swinging or rounding your back.
mistakes: Shrugging the weights up with your traps

name: Face Pulls
muscles: Rear shoulders, upper back, mid traps
setup: Attach a rope to a cable pulley set at about face height, hold an end in each hand with your palms facing in, and step back until your arms are straight and the weight lifts.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft, core braced, and ribs pulled down so you do not lean back.
Pull the rope toward your face, splitting the ends apart as you go, with your elbows high and out to the sides.
Finish with your hands beside your ears and your shoulder blades squeezed, then return slowly until your arms are straight again.
mistakes: Using so much weight that you lean back
Pulling the rope down to your chest
Letting your elbows drop below your hands

name: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press
muscles: Front and side shoulders, triceps, core
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell at each shoulder with your palms facing forward and your elbows just in front of your body.
steps: Squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and pull your ribs down so your torso stays tall with no lean back.
Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are straight and the weights are over your shoulders, with your ribs staying down.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to your shoulders, keeping your knees soft and your legs still so only your arms do the work.
cues: Only your arms do the work
mistakes: Leaning back to push the weights up
Bouncing with your legs to help

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
muscles: Front and side shoulders, triceps, side core
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding one dumbbell at your shoulder with your palm facing forward and your free hand resting on your hip.
steps: Take a breath, tighten your core, and stack your ribs over your hips, staying tall instead of leaning away from the weight.
Press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is straight and the weight is over your shoulder.
Lower it slowly back to your shoulder. Finish all your reps on this arm, then switch sides and repeat.
mistakes: Leaning sideways away from the weight
Flaring your ribs as you press
Letting the dumbbell drift out in front

name: Arnold Press
muscles: Front, side and rear shoulders, triceps
setup: Sit on a bench with an upright back pad, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your chest with your palms facing you and your elbows pointing down.
steps: Press your back into the pad, brace your core, and pull your ribs down so your lower back stays flat.
Start pressing the dumbbells up, and as they pass your chin, turn your palms outward and swing your elbows out to the sides.
Finish with your arms straight overhead and your palms facing forward, with your ribs still down.
Reverse the motion slowly, turning your palms back toward you as the dumbbells lower to the front of your chest.
mistakes: Using weights too heavy to rotate smoothly

name: Push Press
setup: Take a barbell from a rack with an overhand grip just outside your shoulders, rest it on your front shoulders, and stand with your feet hip-width apart and your elbows slightly forward.
steps: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and dip a short way by bending your knees, keeping your torso upright and your heels down.
Drive your feet into the floor and straighten your legs fast, using that speed to launch the bar upward.
As the bar leaves your shoulders, finish pressing with your arms until they lock out overhead, with your ribs still pulled down.
Lower the bar to your shoulders, bending your knees slightly to catch the weight, and reset your brace before the next rep.
mistakes: Pressing before your legs finish driving
Letting your ribs flare open overhead

name: Machine Shoulder Press
setup: Adjust the seat of the shoulder press machine so the handles are level with your shoulders, sit with your back flat against the pad, and take hold of the handles.
steps: Plant your feet flat, brace your core, and keep your ribs down with your back resting against the pad.
Press the handles up until your arms are almost straight, without shrugging your shoulders toward your ears.
Lower the handles slowly until your hands are about shoulder height, keeping your back on the pad the whole time.
mistakes: Seat set too low or too high
Arching your back off the pad

name: Landmine Press
muscles: Front shoulders, upper chest, triceps, core
setup: Secure one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or a corner, then stand facing it and hold the loaded end at your shoulder with one hand.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart or one foot slightly ahead, your elbow tucked near your side, your core braced, and your ribs down.
Press the end of the bar up and forward in a smooth arc until your arm is straight, with your body staying in one straight line.
Lower the bar slowly to your shoulder, keeping your hips and chest square. Finish your reps on this arm, then switch.
mistakes: Twisting your torso as you press
Leaning back to push the bar
Hiking your shoulder up as you press

name: Cable Lateral Raises
setup: Set a cable pulley to its lowest position with a single handle, stand sideways to the machine, and hold the handle in the hand farthest from it, across the front of your body.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, brace your core, pull your ribs down, and keep a small bend in your working elbow.
Raise your arm out to the side in an arc, leading with your elbow, until your hand reaches about shoulder height.
Lower slowly back across your body, keeping the cable tight, then finish your reps and turn around to switch arms.
mistakes: Leaning away to swing the handle up
Letting your shoulder rise to help
Letting the weight rest between reps

name: Leaning Lateral Raises
setup: Hold a sturdy upright or rack post with one hand, lean your whole body away from it, and hold a dumbbell in your free hand, letting it hang straight down.
steps: Lean out from your ankles with your body in one straight line, brace your core, and keep your ribs down.
Raise the dumbbell out to the side, leading with your elbow, until your hand reaches about shoulder height.
Lower slowly until the dumbbell hangs away from your side again, finish your reps, then turn around and switch arms.
mistakes: Bending at the waist to lean
Leaning so far that you lose balance

name: Front Raises
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with your palms facing your body.
steps: Tuck your ribs down toward your hips and tighten your core so your torso stays still.
Raise both dumbbells straight in front of you with a small bend in your elbows until your hands reach about shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower the weights slowly back to your thighs without swinging or leaning back.
mistakes: Swinging the weights up with your body
Raising the weights above shoulder height

name: Plate Front Raises
setup: Stand tall holding a weight plate in front of your thighs with both hands on its sides, as if you were holding a steering wheel.
steps: Squeeze the plate, tighten your core, and pull your ribs down so your body stays tall and still.
Raise the plate straight in front of you, with a small bend in your elbows, until your hands reach about shoulder height.
Pause for a moment, then lower the plate slowly back to your thighs without leaning back.
mistakes: Leaning back to lift the plate
Using a plate you cannot control

name: Reverse Pec Deck
muscles: Rear shoulders, upper back, mid traps
setup: Sit facing the pad of a pec deck machine with your chest against it, adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height, and hold them with your arms straight in front of you.
steps: Keep your chest pressed to the pad, your ribs down, and a small bend in your elbows, with your shoulders relaxed away from your ears.
Pull the handles out and back in a wide arc until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your upper back briefly, then let the handles return slowly without letting the weight stack rest between reps.
mistakes: Pulling with your hands instead of elbows
Letting the weight stack slam down

name: Cable Rear Delt Flys
muscles: Rear shoulders, upper back, mid traps
setup: Set both cable pulleys to shoulder height with single handles, stand in the middle, and grab the right handle with your left hand and the left handle with your right hand.
steps: Step back until the cables are tight, stand with your knees soft and feet hip-width apart, and brace your core with your ribs pulled down.
With a small bend in your elbows, pull your arms apart and back in a wide arc until your hands are out to your sides.
Squeeze your upper back for a moment, then bring the handles back together slowly, keeping tension on the cables the whole way.
mistakes: Leaning back to pull the handles
Bending your elbows into a row

name: Upright Rows
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, your hands about shoulder-width apart and your arms straight.
steps: Tighten your core and glutes, keep your ribs stacked over your hips, and stand tall with your chest up.
Lead with your elbows and pull the bar up close to your body until your elbows reach about shoulder height.
Pause for a moment, then lower the bar slowly along the same path until your arms are straight again.
mistakes: Raising your elbows above shoulder height
Letting the bar drift away from you
Swinging the bar up with your hips

name: Pike Push-Ups
muscles: Front and side shoulders, triceps, upper chest
setup: Start on your hands and feet with your hips lifted high so your body makes an upside-down V, your hands slightly wider than your shoulders, and your legs as straight as you can.
steps: Walk your feet in until your hips are high, press the floor away, and pull your ribs down so your back stays long and flat.
Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands, keeping your elbows angled back at about forty-five degrees.
Press the floor away to straighten your arms, pushing your hips back and up to return to the start.
mistakes: Hips dropping into a regular push-up

name: Handstand Push-Ups
setup: Place your hands on the floor about a foot from a wall, shoulder-width apart with a folded mat between them, then kick up one leg at a time until your heels rest on the wall.
steps: Squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and pull your ribs down so your body makes one straight line from your hands to your heels.
Bend your elbows and lower slowly until the top of your head lightly touches the mat, with your elbows angled back at about forty-five degrees.
Press the floor away hard until your arms are straight again, keeping your body in the same tight line.
When your set is finished, bring one foot down at a time with control and rest before the next set.
cues: One straight line to your heels
mistakes: Arching your back into the wall
Trying it before pike push-ups feel easy

name: Kettlebell Press
muscles: Front and side shoulders, triceps, core
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell by the handle at your shoulder in the rack position, with the bell resting on the back of your forearm and your elbow tucked in.
steps: Lock in your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your ribs tucked down, with your wrist straight so the bell stays against your forearm.
Press the kettlebell straight up until your arm is straight and your upper arm is close to your ear.
Lower it slowly back to the rack position. Finish all your reps on this arm, then switch sides and repeat.
mistakes: Pressing the bell out in front

name: Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Press
muscles: Shoulders, grip and forearms, triceps, core
setup: Hold a light kettlebell upside down by the handle at your shoulder, with the bell pointing straight up, your wrist straight, and your elbow tucked near your ribs.
steps: Squeeze the handle as hard as you can, brace your core, and pull your ribs down while you balance the bell above your fist.
Press the kettlebell straight up, keeping the bell level and your wrist stacked over your elbow, until your arm is straight.
Lower it slowly back to your shoulder without letting the bell tip, then finish your reps and switch arms.
mistakes: Starting with a weight that is too heavy

name: Y Raises
muscles: Rear and side shoulders, lower traps, upper back
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about forty-five degrees, lie face down on it with your chest on the pad and your toes on the floor, and hold a very light dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging down.
steps: Brace your core, keep your ribs down, and look at the floor so your neck stays in line with your spine.
With your thumbs up and a small bend in your elbows, raise both arms forward and up into a Y shape, in line with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades down and back at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly back to the start.
cues: Thumbs up, arms in a Y
Ribs down, chest on the pad
mistakes: Lifting your chest off the pad

name: Band Pull-Aparts
muscles: Rear shoulders, upper back, mid traps
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a resistance band in front of you at shoulder height with your arms straight, your palms facing down, and your hands about shoulder-width apart.
steps: Draw your ribs down, tighten your core, and stand tall so you do not lean back.
Pull the band apart by moving your hands out to your sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together until your arms form a T.
Pause for a moment, then bring your hands back together slowly, keeping tension on the band the whole time.

name: Cuban Press
muscles: Rotator cuff, rear and side shoulders, upper traps
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a very light dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with an overhand grip and your arms straight.
steps: Brace your core, pull your ribs down, and lift the dumbbells up your body like an upright row, with your elbows leading out to the sides.
When your elbows reach shoulder height, rotate your forearms upward until the dumbbells point at the ceiling, keeping your upper arms level.
Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are straight, keeping your ribs down and your neck relaxed.
Reverse the whole path slowly, lowering the weights, rotating them back down, and bringing them to your thighs.
mistakes: Using weights that are too heavy
Dropping your elbows during the rotation

name: Lu Raises
muscles: Front and side shoulders, upper traps, upper back
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a very light dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with your arms straight and your palms facing your body.
steps: Squeeze your glutes, tighten your core, and keep your ribs from flaring open while your arms travel overhead.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, raise the dumbbells forward and out in a wide arc, letting your palms turn to face forward as they rise.
Finish with your arms overhead in a wide Y shape and your biceps close to your ears, without arching your back.
Reverse the same arc slowly, lowering the dumbbells back to the front of your thighs.
cues: Wide arc up to a Y
mistakes: Arching your back to get overhead
Choosing weights that are too heavy

name: Wall Slides
setup: Stand with your back, hips, and head against a wall and your feet a short step out, with your elbows out at shoulder height and bent to ninety degrees, and the backs of your hands on the wall.
steps: Brace your core and gently pull your ribs down so your lower back stays close to the wall.
Slowly slide your arms up the wall into a Y shape, keeping your elbows, wrists, and hands touching the wall for as long as you can.
Slide back down to the start with control, keeping your head and back against the wall the whole time.
cues: Ribs down, back on the wall
mistakes: Arching your lower back off the wall
Letting your hands leave the wall
Hunching your shoulders as you slide

name: Scaption Raises
muscles: Front and side shoulders, rotator cuff, upper traps
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your thumbs pointing forward.
steps: Tuck your ribs down toward your hips, keep your core tight, and let your shoulders relax away from your ears.
Raise both arms halfway between a front raise and a side raise, keeping your thumbs up, until your hands reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower slowly along the same angle without letting your shoulders shrug up.

name: Pull-Ups
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands just wider than your shoulders and palms facing away, with your arms straight and your feet off the floor.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down and back, then drive your elbows toward your ribs to lift your chest up toward the bar.
Keep pulling until your chin clears the bar, with your legs still and your body in a straight line.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are completely straight, then start the next rep from a full hang. You've got this!
cues: Pull your elbows to your ribs
mistakes: Shrugging your shoulders up to your ears

name: Barbell Bent-Over Rows
muscles: Lats, mid back, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip just wider than your shoulders, soften your knees, and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is about forty-five degrees and the bar hangs below your shoulders.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat and your neck long, and look at the floor a few feet in front of you.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows back, keeping them about forty-five degrees from your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a moment, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Hold the same torso angle on every rep, so your back does the pulling instead of your hips jerking the bar. Strong and steady.
mistakes: Standing up to jerk the bar
Letting the bar swing away from you

name: Lat Pulldowns
muscles: Lats, upper back, biceps, rear shoulders
setup: Sit at a lat pulldown machine, tuck your thighs under the pads, and reach up to hold the wide bar with an overhand grip, hands a little wider than your shoulders.
steps: Lean back slightly, lift your chest, and pull your shoulder blades down before the bar starts to move.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back toward your hips.
Pause for a moment, then let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight and you feel a stretch in your lats.
mistakes: Pulling the bar behind your neck
Shrugging your shoulders up to your ears

name: Seated Cable Rows
muscles: Mid back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Sit at a low cable row station with your feet on the platform and your knees slightly bent, and hold the V-handle with your arms straight and your back tall.
steps: Sit tall with your chest up, brace your core, and keep your back flat, leaning forward only slightly from your hips.
Pull the handle to your lower stomach, driving your elbows straight back along your sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment, then let your arms straighten slowly, keeping your chest tall instead of rounding forward.
mistakes: Rounding your back at the stretch
Shrugging your shoulders as you pull

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Rows
muscles: Lats, mid back, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Place your left hand and left knee on a flat bench, plant your right foot on the floor beside it, and hold a dumbbell in your right hand with your arm hanging straight down.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat and parallel to the floor, and keep your neck in line with your spine.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, driving your elbow back and up and keeping it close to your side.
Squeeze your shoulder blade toward your spine at the top, then lower the dumbbell slowly until your arm is straight.
Finish all your reps on this side, then switch hands and knees and repeat on the other side.
cues: Pull your elbow to your hip

name: Chin-Ups
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an underhand grip, palms facing you and hands shoulder-width apart, so your biceps share the work with your back.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down and back, then bend your elbows and pull your chest up toward the bar, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Keep pulling until your chin is over the bar, and squeeze your biceps and back for a moment at the top.
Lower yourself under control until your arms are completely straight, without swinging, then start the next rep. Nice and controlled.
cues: Elbows stay close to your sides
mistakes: Dropping fast on the way down

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Ups
muscles: Outer lats, upper back, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands about one and a half times shoulder-width apart, with your arms straight and your feet off the floor.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down and back, then drive your elbows down and out toward your sides as you pull yourself up.
Keep pulling until your chin clears the bar, aiming your upper chest at it and keeping your chest tall.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight, without letting your shoulders shrug up toward your ears. Take your time.
mistakes: Hands set too wide to control

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Ups
setup: Grab the parallel handles of a pull-up station with your palms facing each other, then hang with your arms straight and your feet off the floor.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down and back, then bend your elbows and pull yourself up, sliding your elbows down along your sides.
Keep pulling until your chin is above the handles, with your chest tall and your palms still facing each other.
Lower slowly until your arms are completely straight, then start the next rep without swinging.

name: Assisted Pull-Ups
setup: Pick a weight on the assisted pull-up machine, where more weight means more help, kneel on the pad, and take the handles with an overhand grip just wider than your shoulders.
steps: Let your arms hang straight, then pull your shoulder blades down and back to begin the lift.
Bend your elbows and pull your chest toward the handles until your chin is above them, driving your elbows down toward your ribs.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight again, and as you get stronger, pick less weight to get less help. Nice work!

name: Scapular Pull-Ups
muscles: Lower traps, lats, muscles around the shoulder blades
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands just wider than your shoulders, with your arms completely straight and your feet off the floor.
steps: Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and back so your body rises about an inch or two.
Pause for a second at the top, with your arms still straight and your shoulders pulled down, away from your ears.
Slowly let your shoulder blades rise again until you are in a full hang, then repeat.
mistakes: Moving too fast to feel it

name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldowns
setup: Sit at a lat pulldown machine with your thighs under the pads, attach a close-grip V-handle to the cable, and hold it with your palms facing each other.
steps: Lean back slightly, lift your chest, and pull your shoulder blades down before you start the pull.
Pull the handle to your upper chest, sliding your elbows down along your sides instead of out wide.
Squeeze your back for a moment, then let the handle rise slowly until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Swinging your torso back and forth
Letting the handle yank you up

name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldowns
setup: Sit at a lat pulldown machine with your thighs under the pads, and hold the straight bar with an underhand grip, palms facing you and hands shoulder-width apart.
steps: Lean back slightly, lift your chest, and pull your shoulder blades down before the bar starts to move.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides so your biceps and lower lats share the work.
Squeeze for a moment, then let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.
cues: Elbows stay close to your sides
Chest up to meet the bar
mistakes: Leaning back to heave the weight

name: Straight-Arm Pulldowns
setup: Stand facing a high cable pulley with a straight bar attached, step back a few feet, and hold the bar overhand with your arms reaching forward and slightly up, elbows softly bent.
steps: Hinge forward slightly at your hips, brace your core, and keep the same soft bend in your elbows all the way through.
Sweep the bar down in a wide arc until it reaches your thighs, using your lats and not your arms.
Squeeze your lats for a second, then let the bar rise slowly until you feel a stretch under your arms.
cues: Sweep the bar to your thighs
mistakes: Bending your elbows into a pushdown
Letting the weight snap back up

name: Band Pulldowns
setup: Loop a resistance band over a pull-up bar, kneel on the floor facing it, and hold an end of the band in each hand with your arms reaching up a little wider than your shoulders.
steps: Kneel tall with your chest up, brace your core, and pull your shoulder blades down before you start to pull.
Pull your hands down toward your shoulders by driving your elbows down and back, squeezing your back muscles.
Let the band pull your hands back up slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your ribs down.

name: Pendlay Rows
muscles: Lats, mid back, rear shoulders, lower back
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a barbell on the floor over your midfoot, then hinge until your back is flat and nearly parallel to the floor and grip the bar overhand, wider than your shoulders.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat and your neck long, and look at the floor just ahead of your hands.
Pull the bar from the floor to your lower chest in one quick, strong pull, driving your elbows up and back.
Lower the bar with control until it rests on the floor, with your arms straight.
Pause for a second to reset your brace and your back position, then start the next rep from a dead stop. Stay patient.
mistakes: Rising up to heave the bar
Letting the bar bounce off the floor

name: Underhand Barbell Rows
muscles: Lower lats, mid back, biceps, lower back
setup: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, soften your knees, and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is about forty-five degrees.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat and your neck long, and let the bar hang below your shoulders with your arms straight.
Pull the bar toward your lower belly, keeping your elbows close to your sides as they drive back and up.
Squeeze your back and biceps for a moment, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Standing up to swing the bar

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Rows
muscles: Mid back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about forty-five degrees, lie face down on it with your chest against the pad and your feet on the floor, and let a dumbbell in each hand hang straight down.
steps: Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down, and keep your chest pressed into the pad for the whole set.
Row both dumbbells up toward the sides of your ribs, driving your elbows back about forty-five degrees from your body.
Squeeze your back for a second at the top, then lower the weights slowly until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Lifting your chest off the pad
Shrugging your shoulders toward your ears

name: Gorilla Rows
muscles: Lats, mid back, rear shoulders, biceps, core
setup: Place two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, stand with your feet wider than your shoulders, hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, and grip one handle in each hand.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat, and push your hips back so your chest stays low and steady.
Row one kettlebell up toward your hip, driving your elbow behind you, while the other kettlebell stays on the floor.
Set it down softly, then row the other kettlebell the same way; one row on each side is one rep.

name: Kroc Rows
setup: Stand beside a bench or rack in a staggered stance, rest your free hand on it, hinge forward until your back is nearly parallel to the floor, and hold a heavy but controllable dumbbell in your other hand.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat and your neck long, and let the dumbbell hang straight below your shoulder.
Row the dumbbell up toward your hip in one smooth pull, allowing only a small push from your legs to keep it moving.
Lower the dumbbell until your arm is straight and feel your lat stretch, then keep going for a long set before switching sides. Stay strong.
mistakes: Weight so heavy your form breaks

name: Wide-Grip Seated Rows
muscles: Upper back, rear shoulders, lats, biceps
setup: Sit at a low cable row station with your feet on the platform and your knees slightly bent, and hold a wide bar with an overhand grip, hands well outside your shoulders.
steps: Sit tall with your chest up, brace your core, and keep your back flat.
Pull the bar to your lower chest, letting your elbows flare out wide and travel straight back, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly, then let your arms straighten slowly while you keep your back tall.
cues: Pull the bar to your chest
mistakes: Pulling too low toward your belly

name: Single-Arm Cable Rows
muscles: Lats, mid back, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Sit at a low cable row station with a single D-handle attached, place your feet on the platform with your knees slightly bent, and hold the handle in one hand with your arm straight.
steps: Sit tall, brace your core, and keep your shoulders square to the machine so your body does not twist.
Pull the handle to the side of your waist, driving your elbow straight back along your side.
Squeeze your shoulder blade toward your spine, then let your arm straighten slowly; finish your reps, then switch hands.

name: T-Bar Rows
muscles: Lats, mid back, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Wedge one end of a loaded barbell into a corner or landmine, straddle the bar facing the plates, hinge forward to about forty-five degrees, and hold a V-handle hooked under the bar near the plates.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat and your neck long, and let the plates hang with your arms straight.
Pull the handle toward your lower chest, driving your elbows back and keeping them close to your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top, then lower the plates slowly until your arms are straight.
Keep your torso at the same angle on every rep, without standing up to help the lift.
mistakes: Standing up to heave the weight
Shrugging your shoulders to your ears

name: Landmine Rows
muscles: Lats, mid back, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Wedge one end of a loaded barbell into a corner or landmine, face the plates in a staggered stance, hinge forward with your free hand on your front thigh, and hold the bar near the plates with one hand.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat and your neck long, and let the bar hang at arm's length.
Pull the bar up toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your side as you drive it back and up.
Squeeze your shoulder blade toward your spine, then lower slowly until your arm is straight; finish your reps, then switch sides.

name: Meadows Rows
muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Wedge one end of a loaded barbell into a landmine, stand side-on to the plates in a staggered stance, hinge forward with your free hand on your front knee, and grip the end of the bar overhand.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat and your neck long, and let the end of the bar hang so you feel a deep stretch in your back.
Pull the bar up and back toward your hip, letting your elbow flare out to about forty-five degrees from your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blade toward your spine, then lower slowly until your arm is straight; finish your reps, then switch sides.

name: Inverted Rows
muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Set a barbell in a rack or Smith machine at about waist height, lie under it, grip the bar overhand just wider than your shoulders, and hang with straight arms, your heels on the floor, and your body in a straight line.
steps: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so your body stays in one straight line from your heels to your head.
Pull your chest up to the bar by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause with your chest at the bar, then lower slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your body in that same line.
To make it easier, bend your knees and plant your feet flat on the floor.
cues: Touch your chest to the bar

name: Machine Rows
muscles: Mid back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Sit at a seated row machine with your chest against the pad, adjust the seat so the handles line up with your chest, and grab them with your arms straight.
steps: Sit tall with your chest on the pad, brace your core, and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Pull the handles toward your ribs, driving your elbows straight back past your body, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a second, then let the handles return slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your chest on the pad.

name: High Rows
muscles: Lats, upper back, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Sit at a high row machine with your chest against the pad, adjust the seat so the handles are just above your head, and reach up to take them with your arms nearly straight.
steps: Sit tall with your chest on the pad, brace your core, and pull your shoulder blades down.
Pull the handles down and back, driving your elbows toward the floor until your hands are beside your upper chest.
Squeeze your back for a second, then let the handles rise slowly until your arms are nearly straight.
mistakes: Shrugging your shoulders as you pull
Letting the handles yank you up

name: Seal Rows
muscles: Mid back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Lie face down on a high, flat bench, such as one raised on sturdy blocks, with a loaded barbell on the floor beneath you, and grip the bar overhand wider than your shoulders.
steps: Press your chest into the bench, keep your neck long, and squeeze your shoulder blades back and down before you pull.
Row the bar up until it touches the bench, driving your elbows back about forty-five degrees from your body.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your legs still and your chest on the bench.
cues: Touch the bar to the bench
mistakes: Lifting your chest off the bench

name: Renegade Rows
muscles: Lats, mid back, core, shoulders, biceps
setup: Get into a high plank with your hands on two hex dumbbells under your shoulders and your feet wide apart, with your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.
steps: Brace your abs, squeeze your glutes, and push the floor away so your body stays straight and stable.
Row one dumbbell up toward your ribs, driving your elbow back, while your hips stay square to the floor.
Place that dumbbell down softly, then row the other side; one row on each side is one rep.
mistakes: Hips twisting open as you row
Using dumbbells that are too heavy

name: Band Rows
muscles: Mid back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps
setup: Sit on the floor with your legs out in front and your knees slightly bent, loop a resistance band around your feet, and hold an end of the band in each hand with your arms straight.
steps: Sit tall with your chest up, brace your core, and keep your back flat.
Pull your hands toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back along your sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a second, then let your arms straighten slowly while you stay tall and keep tension in the band.

name: Deadlifts
muscles: Glutes, hamstrings, lower back, upper back, grip
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a barbell loaded with a weight you can control over the middle of your feet, almost touching your shins.
steps: Hinge your hips back, bend your knees, and grip the bar just outside your legs with straight arms, a flat back, and your chest lifted.
Take a deep breath, brace your core as if someone were about to punch you, and pull the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor away with your legs, keeping the bar against your body, so your hips and shoulders rise together until you stand tall.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without leaning back, then push your hips back and lower the bar down your legs under control. You've got this!
mistakes: Bar drifting away from your legs

name: Rack Pulls
muscles: Upper back, traps, glutes, lower back, grip
setup: Set the pins or safety arms of a power rack so a loaded barbell rests just below knee height, then stand with the bar over your midfoot and your feet hip-width apart.
steps: Hinge your hips back, bend your knees slightly, and grip the bar just outside your legs with straight arms, a flat back, and your chest lifted.
Take a deep breath, brace your core hard, pull your shoulder blades down and back, and pull the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor away and stand tall with the bar close to your legs, then squeeze your glutes and upper back without leaning back.
Push your hips back and lower the bar along your legs until it rests on the pins, then reset your brace for the next rep.
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the pins

name: Trap Bar Deadlifts
setup: Stand inside a loaded trap bar with your feet hip-width apart, then sit your hips back and bend your knees to grip the two handles at your sides.
steps: Lift your chest and keep your back flat; standing inside the bar lets your torso stay more upright than with a barbell deadlift.
Take a deep breath, brace your core, and pull the slack out of your arms.
Push the floor away with your feet so your hips and shoulders rise together until you stand tall.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without leaning back, then push your hips back and lower the bar to the floor under control.

name: Back Extensions
setup: Set the pad of a back extension bench just below your hips, hook your heels under the rollers, and cross your arms over your chest with your body in a straight line.
steps: Brace your core, keep your spine long and neutral, and look at the floor so your neck stays in line.
Hinge forward at your hips and lower your upper body slowly until you feel a stretch in the back of your thighs, keeping your back flat.
Squeeze your glutes to raise your body until it forms a straight line from your head to your heels, then stop.
mistakes: Leaning back past a straight line
Rounding your back at the bottom

name: Reverse Hyperextensions
setup: Lie face down along a flat bench with your hips at the end and your legs hanging off, and hold the bench with both hands to stay in place.
steps: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips pressed into the bench and your neck long.
Raise both legs together, with your knees straight or slightly bent, until they are in line with your body, but no higher.
Pause for a second, then lower your legs slowly until they hang straight down again, without swinging.
mistakes: Swinging your legs up with momentum
Lifting your legs above your back

name: Supermans
muscles: Lower back, glutes, upper back, rear shoulders
setup: Lie face down on a mat with your arms stretched out in front of you, your legs straight, and your head in line with your spine.
steps: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes, keeping your neck long and your eyes on the floor.
Raise your arms, chest, and legs a few inches off the floor at the same time, reaching long through your fingers and toes.
Hold for two seconds, then lower slowly and relax for a moment before the next rep.
cues: Reach long with arms and legs
mistakes: Lifting so high you arch hard

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
setup: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under a barbell on the rack, feet flat on the floor, and your hands gripping the bar about shoulder width apart.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back and down, unrack the bar, and hold it over your chest with straight arms and your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Breathe in, brace your core, and lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Press the bar up until your arms are straight, squeezing your triceps at the top and keeping your elbows tucked.
Guide the bar back into the hooks before letting go, and use a spotter when the weight gets heavy.
cues: Elbows tucked close to your sides
Squeeze your triceps at the top
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off your chest

name: Rope Triceps Pushdowns
setup: Attach a rope to a high pulley, stand facing the machine with your feet hip width apart, grip the rope with your palms facing each other, and pin your elbows to your sides.
steps: Lean forward slightly, brace your core, and bend your elbows so your hands are near your chest with your upper arms pinned to your sides.
Push the rope straight down until your arms are fully straight, then pull the two ends apart at the bottom and squeeze your triceps.
Let your hands rise slowly back up until your forearms are about level with the floor, keeping your elbows still the whole time.
cues: Spread the rope at the bottom
mistakes: Leaning over the weight to push it

name: Skull Crushers
setup: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, hold an EZ curl bar with a shoulder width overhand grip, and press it straight up over your chest with your arms straight.
steps: Brace your core, pull your shoulder blades back, and keep your upper arms pointing straight up or tilted slightly back toward your head.
Bend only your elbows to lower the bar slowly until it is a few inches above your forehead, with your elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Straighten your elbows to press the bar back up to the start, squeezing your triceps at the top without letting your elbows flare out.
mistakes: Swinging your upper arms to lift
Going too heavy to control the bar

name: Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extensions
setup: Sit on a bench with back support or stand tall with your feet hip width apart, and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands cupped under the top plate and your arms straight.
steps: Brace your core, tuck your ribs down so your back stays neutral, and point your elbows toward the ceiling with your biceps close to your ears.
Bend only your elbows to lower the dumbbell slowly behind your head until you feel a stretch in the back of your arms.
Straighten your elbows to press the dumbbell back up until your arms are straight overhead, squeezing your triceps at the top.

name: Parallel Bar Dips
setup: Grip the parallel bars of a dip station, press up until your arms are straight, and keep your body upright with your chest lifted and your legs hanging straight down or crossed behind you.
steps: Keep your torso upright, your elbows tucked close to your sides, and your shoulders pressed down away from your ears.
Bend your elbows and lower your body slowly until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, with your elbows pointing straight back.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms and rise back up, squeezing your triceps at the top without shrugging.

name: Straight-Bar Triceps Pushdowns
setup: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley, stand facing the machine with your feet hip width apart, grip the bar with your hands shoulder width apart and palms down, and pin your elbows to your sides.
steps: Lean forward slightly, brace your core, and bring the bar to about chest height with your elbows bent to ninety degrees and tucked at your sides.
Push the bar straight down until your arms are fully straight, keeping your wrists straight and squeezing your triceps at the bottom.
Let the bar rise slowly back to chest height, moving only your forearms while your elbows and shoulders stay still.
mistakes: Elbows flaring away from your sides
Wrists bending backward under the load
Bouncing the bar up with your body

name: Reverse-Grip Triceps Pushdowns
setup: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley, stand facing the machine, grip the bar with an underhand grip about shoulder width apart, and pin your elbows to your sides.
steps: Lean forward slightly, brace your core, and bring the bar to chest height with your palms facing up and your elbows tucked at your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight, keeping your wrists firm and in line with your forearms, and squeeze your triceps.
Let the bar rise slowly until your forearms are about level with the floor, keeping your elbows pinned and your palms facing the ceiling.
mistakes: Elbows swinging away from your ribs

name: Single-Arm Cable Pushdowns
setup: Attach a single handle to a high pulley, stand facing the machine with your feet hip width apart, grip the handle with one hand, and pin that elbow to your side.
steps: Lean forward slightly, brace your core, and bend your working elbow to ninety degrees, with your free hand resting on your hip for balance.
Push the handle straight down until your arm is fully straight, keeping your elbow pinned and your wrist straight, and squeeze your triceps.
Let your hand rise slowly back to chest height, finish all your reps on this arm, and then switch sides.
mistakes: Twisting your torso to push down

name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extensions
setup: Attach a rope to a low pulley, face away from the machine with the rope held behind your head, and step forward into a staggered stance with your elbows bent and pointing up.
steps: Brace your core, lean forward slightly, and tuck your ribs down so your back stays neutral, with your elbows pointing up beside your ears.
Straighten your elbows to press the rope forward and up until your arms are fully straight, then pull the rope ends apart and squeeze.
Bend your elbows slowly to let the rope return behind your head, keeping your elbows pointed up and still.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out to the sides
Letting the cable pull you backward

name: Overhead Band Triceps Extensions
setup: Stand on one end of a long resistance band, hold the other end in both hands, and bring your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing up.
steps: Brace your core, tuck your ribs down so your back stays neutral, and keep your elbows pointing at the ceiling, close to your ears.
Straighten your elbows to press your hands up toward the ceiling against the band until your arms are fully straight overhead.
Bend your elbows slowly to lower your hands back behind your head, keeping your upper arms still and resisting the band the whole way.
mistakes: Letting the band yank your hands down

name: Dumbbell Skull Crushers
setup: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand, then press the weights straight up over your chest with your palms facing each other.
steps: Brace your core, pull your shoulder blades back, and keep your upper arms pointing straight up, with your elbows close together.
Bend only your elbows to lower the dumbbells slowly down beside your head, until they are level with your ears and you feel a stretch.
Straighten your elbows to press the dumbbells back up over your chest, keeping your upper arms still and your wrists straight.
mistakes: Lowering the weights toward your face
Using weights too heavy to control

name: Triceps Kickbacks
setup: Stand with a dumbbell in your right hand, hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, rest your left hand on a bench or thigh, and tuck your right elbow beside your ribs.
steps: Bend your knees slightly, brace your core, and raise your upper arm until it is in line with your back, with your elbow bent to ninety degrees.
Straighten your elbow to press the dumbbell back until your arm is fully straight, keeping your upper arm still and squeezing your triceps at the end.
Bend your elbow slowly to bring the dumbbell back to the start, finish all your reps on this arm, and then switch.
cues: Upper arm stays glued in place

name: Cable Triceps Kickbacks
setup: Attach a single handle to a low pulley, stand facing the machine and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, hold the handle in one hand, and tuck that elbow beside your ribs.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat, and lift your upper arm in line with your back, with your elbow bent to ninety degrees.
Straighten your elbow to press the handle back until your arm is fully straight, keeping your upper arm still and squeezing your triceps.
Bend your elbow slowly to let the handle come back to the start, fighting the cable the whole way, then switch arms after your reps.
cues: Upper arm level with your back
mistakes: Standing up tall during the set

name: Bench Dips
setup: Sit on the edge of a sturdy bench with your hands gripping the edge beside your hips, walk your feet out with your knees bent, and slide your hips off the bench.
steps: Straighten your arms to hold your body up, keeping your shoulders down away from your ears, your chest lifted, and your hips close to the bench.
Bend your elbows straight back, not out to the sides, and lower your body until your upper arms are about parallel with the floor.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms and lift your body back up, squeezing your triceps at the top.
mistakes: Flaring your elbows out to the sides
Hips drifting far from the bench

name: Diamond Push-Ups
setup: Start in a high plank on the floor, then bring your hands together under your chest with your thumbs and index fingers touching to make a diamond shape, and set your feet hip width apart.
steps: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so your body is one straight line from your head to your heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward your hands, keeping your elbows close to your sides, until your chest is just above your hands.
Press the floor away until your arms are straight, squeezing your triceps at the top and keeping your hips from sagging.
mistakes: Hands too far in front of you

name: Close-Grip Push-Ups
setup: Start in a high plank on the floor with your hands under your chest and just inside shoulder width, and your feet hip width apart.
steps: Squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and look at a spot on the floor just ahead of your hands so your neck stays long.
Lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows brushing past your ribs and pointing straight back, until your chest is a few inches above the floor.
Press the floor away until your arms are straight, keeping your elbows tucked and your hips level the whole time.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out to the sides
Hands set too close to stay stable

name: JM Press
setup: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under a barbell on the rack, feet flat on the floor, and hands gripping the bar just inside shoulder width, with a spotter ready behind you.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back, unrack the bar, and hold it over your chest with straight arms and your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Lower the bar slowly toward your upper chest by bending your elbows, keeping them tucked in close, and stop a few inches above your chest.
Drive the bar back up along the same path by straightening your elbows, until your arms are straight and your triceps are squeezed.
Guide the bar back into the hooks before you let go, and keep the weight light enough that you stay in full control.
cues: Stop a few inches above chest
mistakes: Letting the bar touch your chest
Going too heavy to control it

name: Tate Press
setup: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand, then press the weights up over your chest with your palms facing your feet.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades back, brace your core, and let your elbows angle out to the sides so your upper arms point up and slightly out.
Bend only your elbows to lower the dumbbells in a short arc until they hover just above your chest, keeping your elbows flared out and still.
Straighten your elbows to press the dumbbells back up to the start, squeezing your triceps at the top and keeping your wrists straight.
mistakes: Letting the dumbbells crash into your chest
Moving your upper arms to press
Starting with weights that are too heavy

name: Band Triceps Pushdowns
setup: Loop a resistance band over a high anchor, such as a pull-up bar, hold both ends at chest height, and stand tall with your elbows pinned to your sides.
steps: Lean forward slightly, brace your core, and bend your elbows to ninety degrees so your hands are near your chest.
Push both hands straight down against the band until your arms are fully straight, keeping your elbows pinned and squeezing your triceps.
Let your hands rise slowly back up, resisting the pull of the band, until your elbows are bent to ninety degrees again.
mistakes: Leaning your body into the push
Letting the band yank your hands up

name: Machine Triceps Extensions
setup: Sit at a triceps extension machine, adjust the seat so your upper arms rest flat on the pad with your elbows lined up with the pivot, and grip the handles.
steps: Sit tall with your back against the pad, shoulders down and feet flat, and keep your upper arms resting on the arm pad the whole time.
Push the handles down and away by straightening your elbows until your arms are fully straight, and squeeze your triceps for a second.
Bend your elbows slowly to let the handles return until you feel a stretch in your triceps, without letting the weight stack crash down.
cues: Upper arms stay on the pad
mistakes: Lifting your elbows off the pad
Shrugging your shoulders toward your ears

name: Dip Machine
setup: Sit in a seated dip machine with your back flat against the pad, adjust the seat so the handles start beside your lower chest, and grip them with your elbows bent and tucked in.
steps: Keep your back against the pad, your chest lifted, and your shoulders pressed down away from your ears throughout the set.
Push the handles down by straightening your elbows until your arms are almost fully straight, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Let the handles rise slowly until your elbows are bent to about ninety degrees, and stop there rather than going deeper.
cues: Press down, elbows by your sides
mistakes: Letting the weight pull you too deep

name: Barbell Curls
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and your arms hanging straight down in front of your thighs.
steps: Pin your elbows to your sides, brace your core, and keep your chest up and your knees soft.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, bending only at your elbows, and squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower the bar slowly for about three seconds until your arms are fully straight, without letting your elbows drift forward.
mistakes: Swinging the bar with your hips

name: Incline Dumbbell Curls
muscles: Biceps with a deep stretch, forearms
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about forty-five degrees, sit back against it with a dumbbell in each hand, and let your arms hang straight down at your sides with your palms facing forward.
steps: Press your shoulders and back into the bench and let your upper arms hang straight down from your shoulders.
Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders, bending only at your elbows, and squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight, feeling the stretch in the front of your arms, and don't let your elbows swing forward.
cues: Feel the stretch at the bottom

name: Hammer Curls
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing each other, as if you were holding hammers.
steps: Pin your elbows to your sides, brace your core, and keep your palms facing each other the whole time.
Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders, bending only at your elbows, with your thumbs pointing up.
