Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are completely straight.
mistakes: Rotating your wrists as you curl

name: Preacher Curls
setup: Adjust a preacher bench so the top of the pad sits under your armpits, rest the backs of your upper arms on it, and hold an EZ-bar with an underhand grip.
steps: Start with your arms almost straight, resting on the pad, and keep your chest and armpits pressed into the pad.
Curl the bar up toward your chin, bending only at your elbows, until your forearms are nearly vertical, and squeeze your biceps.
Lower the bar slowly all the way down, stopping just before your elbows lock out, and keep your upper arms on the pad.
cues: Upper arms stay on the pad
Slow, no bouncing at the bottom
mistakes: Lifting your chest off the pad

name: Concentration Curls
setup: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet wide, lean forward slightly, and hold a dumbbell in one hand with your elbow braced against the inside of your thigh.
steps: Let the dumbbell hang straight down with your arm fully extended, and rest your free hand on your other knee.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, bending only at your elbow, and squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower slowly until your arm is straight, keeping your upper arm against your thigh; finish your reps, then switch arms.
mistakes: Leaning back to swing the weight
Lifting your elbow off your thigh

name: EZ-Bar Curls
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a wavy EZ-bar with your hands on the angled grips and your arms hanging straight down in front of your thighs.
steps: Pin your elbows to your sides and brace your core; the angled grips tilt your palms slightly, so your wrists stay relaxed.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, bending only at your elbows, and squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your elbows by your sides and your chest tall.

name: Dumbbell Curls
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging at your sides and your palms facing forward.
steps: Pin your elbows to your sides, brace your core, and keep your shoulders back and relaxed.
Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders together, bending only at your elbows, and squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower both dumbbells slowly until your arms are completely straight, without swinging your body. Nice and smooth.
cues: Palms up, squeeze at the top

name: Alternating Dumbbell Curls
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging at your sides and your palms facing your thighs.
steps: Pin your elbows to your sides and brace your core, then curl the right dumbbell up, turning your palm to face you as it rises.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower the dumbbell slowly until your arm is straight.
Repeat with your left arm, going back and forth; a curl with each arm counts as one rep.
cues: Turn your palm up while curling
mistakes: Swinging your torso as you curl

name: Cross-Body Hammer Curls
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing your thighs.
steps: Keep your upper arms still, your elbows by your sides, and your core braced.
Curl one dumbbell diagonally across your body toward your opposite shoulder, keeping your palm facing in and your thumb up.
Lower it slowly along the same path, then curl the other arm; one on each side is one rep.

name: Cable Curls
setup: Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley, stand facing the machine a step or two back with your feet hip-width apart, and hold the bar underhand with your arms straight.
steps: Pin your elbows to your sides, brace your core, and stand tall so the cable has steady tension from the start.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, bending only at your elbows, and squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower the bar slowly, keeping the cable tight, until your arms are straight, without leaning back.

name: Spider Curls
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about forty-five degrees, lie face down on it with your chest against the pad and your feet on the floor, and hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging straight down.
steps: Press your chest into the bench and let your arms hang straight down, with your palms facing forward.
Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders, bending only at your elbows, and squeeze your biceps hard at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are completely straight, keeping your upper arms still and your chest on the bench.
mistakes: Lifting your chest off the bench

name: Zottman Curls
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing forward.
steps: Pin your elbows to your sides and curl both dumbbells up to your shoulders with your palms facing you.
At the top, rotate your wrists so your palms face the floor, and keep that overhand grip.
Lower the dumbbells slowly with your palms down until your arms are straight, then turn your palms forward again and repeat.
cues: Turn your palms at the top
Palms down on the way down
mistakes: Using weights too heavy to lower

name: Drag Curls
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, so the bar rests against the front of your thighs.
steps: Keep the bar touching your body, brace your core, and keep your chest up.
Curl the bar up by pulling your elbows back behind your torso, so the bar slides up your thighs, stomach, and chest.
Squeeze your biceps when the bar reaches your lower chest, then lower it slowly back down along the same path.
cues: Drag the bar up your body
mistakes: Letting the bar swing away from you

name: Bayesian Cable Curls
muscles: Biceps with a deep stretch, forearms
setup: Attach a single handle to a low cable pulley, stand with your back to the machine in a staggered stance, and hold the handle with your arm reaching behind you and the cable tight.
steps: Lean forward slightly, brace your core, and let your elbow sit just behind your torso so you feel a stretch in your biceps.
Curl the handle up toward your shoulder, bending only at your elbow, and keep your upper arm back and still.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower slowly back into the stretch; finish your reps, then switch arms.
mistakes: Standing too close to lose tension

name: Band Curls
setup: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with your feet hip-width apart, and hold an end of the band in each hand with your palms facing forward and your arms straight.
steps: Pin your elbows to your sides, brace your core, and keep your chest tall.
Curl your hands up toward your shoulders, bending only at your elbows, and squeeze your biceps as the band gets tighter.
Lower your hands slowly, keeping tension in the band, until your arms are straight.

name: Twenty-One Curls
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a fairly light barbell or EZ-bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and your arms hanging straight down.
steps: Do seven half reps from straight arms up to the point where your elbows are bent at ninety degrees, with no rest between reps.
Right away, do seven half reps from ninety degrees at your elbows up to the top, squeezing your biceps.
Finish with seven full reps from straight arms to the top, keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, then rest. You've got this!
cues: Seven bottom, seven top, seven full
mistakes: Swinging to finish the last reps

name: Wrist Curls
setup: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up, and rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists hanging just past your knees.
steps: Sit tall, keep your forearms pressed against your thighs, and let your wrists bend down so the dumbbells lower toward the floor.
Curl your wrists up, closing your hands and lifting the dumbbells toward the ceiling as high as you can.
Squeeze your forearms for a second, then lower slowly over about two seconds back to the bottom.
cues: Forearms stay flat on your thighs
mistakes: Lifting your forearms off your thighs
Cutting your range of motion short

name: Reverse Wrist Curls
setup: Sit on a bench holding a light dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing down, and rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists hanging just past your knees.
steps: Sit tall with your forearms flat on your thighs and let your hands bend down so the dumbbells hang below your wrists.
Raise the backs of your hands toward the ceiling by bending your wrists up as far as you can, moving only your hands.
Hold for a second at the top, then lower slowly back down, keeping your forearms still.
mistakes: Using a weight that is too heavy

name: Reverse Curls
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip, your hands shoulder-width apart, and your arms straight.
steps: Stand tall, brace your core, and tuck your elbows against your sides with your wrists straight.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, keeping your wrists straight and your elbows pinned in place.
Squeeze at the top for a second, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight again.

name: Farmer's Carry
muscles: Grip and forearms, upper traps, core, glutes
setup: Stand between two heavy dumbbells with your feet hip-width apart, push your hips back with a flat back, and pick them up, one in each hand.
steps: Stand up tall with the dumbbells hanging at your sides, shoulders back and down, chest proud, core braced, and ribs stacked over your hips.
Walk forward in a straight line with short, quick steps, squeezing the handles hard and keeping your body from swaying.
Keep breathing steadily and look straight ahead until time is up, then lower the dumbbells by pushing your hips back with a flat back.
mistakes: Rounding your back to pick up weights

name: Dead Hang
setup: Standing on a step if the bar is high, reach up to a pull-up bar with an overhand grip a little wider than shoulder-width and hang with your arms straight.
steps: Wrap your thumbs around the bar, squeeze it tight, and let your body hang with your feet off the floor.
Draw your shoulders gently down and away from your ears, brace your core, and pull your ribs down so you do not arch your back.
Hold still and breathe slowly until time is up, then step down carefully onto the floor.
mistakes: Letting your shoulders ride up by your ears

name: Plate Pinch
muscles: Pinch grip, thumb and finger muscles, forearms
setup: Stand next to two smooth weight plates resting together, smooth sides facing out, ready to pinch their top edge between your thumb on one side and your fingers on the other.
steps: Push your hips back with a flat back, pinch the plates tightly, and stand up tall holding them at your side with your arm straight.
Keep your shoulders level, your ribs down, and your core braced while you squeeze the plates together for the whole time.
When time is up, set the plates down carefully, then switch hands and repeat.
mistakes: Letting your shoulder sag under the load
Starting with plates that are too heavy

name: Wrist Roller
muscles: Forearm flexors and extensors, grip, front shoulders
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a wrist roller, a short bar with a weighted rope attached, out in front at shoulder height with an overhand grip and the weight hanging down.
steps: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your arms straight out in front of you with your ribs pulled down.
Turn the bar with your wrists, one hand after the other, to wind the rope up and lift the weight all the way to the bar.
Then reverse the direction slowly and let the rope unwind under control until the weight is back down, repeating until time is up.
mistakes: Using your arms instead of your wrists
Starting with too heavy a weight

name: Towel Hang
setup: Drape a long, sturdy towel over a pull-up bar so both ends hang evenly, then reach up and hold one end in each hand with your arms straight.
steps: Squeeze the towel ends tightly, then lift your feet off the floor so your full weight hangs from your hands.
Keep your arms straight, draw your shoulders gently down from your ears, and brace your core with your ribs pulled down.
Hold still, breathing steadily, until time is up, then place your feet back on the floor or step down carefully.
mistakes: Letting the towel slip through your hands

name: Barbell Shrugs
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip just outside your hips and your arms straight.
steps: Stand tall, squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and keep your ribs down with your chest up and your eyes straight ahead.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can, keeping your arms straight.
Pause for a moment at the top, then lower your shoulders slowly all the way down.
mistakes: Bending your elbows to lift the bar

name: Dumbbell Shrugs
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing in and your arms straight.
steps: Stand tall with your chest up, core braced, and ribs down, and let the dumbbells hang by your sides.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can, without bending your elbows.
Squeeze at the top for one second, then lower slowly until your shoulders are all the way down.
cues: Lift your shoulders, not your arms
mistakes: Using your arms to lift the weights
Moving too fast to feel it

name: Trap Bar Shrugs
setup: Stand inside a loaded trap bar with your feet hip-width apart, push your hips back with a flat back, grab the handles, and stand up tall with your arms straight at your sides.
steps: Stand tall with the bar hanging at your sides, your chest up, core braced, ribs down, and your back flat.
Raise your shoulders straight up as high as you can, as if reaching for your ears, with your arms hanging long.
Hold the top for a second, then let your shoulders sink back down under control.
When your set is done, set the bar down by pushing your hips back and lowering it with a flat back.
mistakes: Rounding your back to pick up the bar

name: Cable Shrugs
setup: Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley, stand facing the machine with your feet hip-width apart, and hold the bar in front of your thighs with an overhand grip and straight arms.
steps: Step back slightly so the cable is tight, stand tall with your core braced and ribs down, and keep your chest up.
Shrug up against the pull of the cable, lifting your shoulders straight toward your ears with your arms staying straight.
Squeeze at the top for a second, then lower slowly until your shoulders are all the way down.
mistakes: Letting the weight stack drop quickly

name: Prone Incline Shrugs
muscles: Mid and upper traps, upper back, grip
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about forty-five degrees, lie face down with your chest on the pad and your toes on the floor, and hold a dumbbell in each hand hanging straight down.
steps: Press your chest into the pad, brace your core lightly, and look at the floor so your neck stays in line with your spine.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and up, keeping your arms straight and your chest on the pad.
Hold the squeeze for a second, then lower slowly until your arms hang long again.
mistakes: Peeling your chest away from the pad

name: Behind-the-Back Shrugs
setup: Set a barbell on rack hooks at about hip height, stand with your back to it, take an overhand grip just outside your hips, and stand tall to lift it off the rack.
steps: Step forward a little so the bar clears the rack, then stand tall with your chest up, core braced, and ribs down.
Shrug straight up, keeping your arms straight and the bar close to the backs of your thighs.
Pause at the top with your chest tall, then lower your shoulders slowly without letting the bar drift back.
When you finish, step back and place the bar on the rack hooks under control.
mistakes: Letting the bar swing away from you

name: Smith Machine Shrugs
setup: Set the Smith machine bar at about thigh height, take an overhand grip just outside your thighs, and stand tall to unhook it with your arms straight.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar right in front of your thighs, with your chest up, core braced, and ribs down.
Shrug straight up toward your ears, letting the bar glide along the guide rails while your arms stay straight.
Hold the top for a second, then lower slowly all the way down.
After your last rep, rotate your wrists to hook the bar back on the rack.
mistakes: Using a weight that cuts your range short

name: Snatch-Grip High Pulls
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with a wide overhand grip, wide enough that the bar touches the crease where your thighs meet your hips when you stand tall.
steps: Push your hips back and lower the bar to just above your knees, keeping your back flat, chest up, ribs down, and shoulders over the bar.
Drive your feet into the floor and straighten your hips and knees fast, keeping your arms straight until your legs finish driving.
As you reach full height, shrug hard and pull your elbows up and out to the sides so the bar rises to about chest height.
Lower the bar back to your thighs under control and reset your hips-back position before the next rep.
cues: Arms stay long until hips finish
mistakes: Pulling with your arms too early
Rounding your back on the way down
Using more weight than you can control

name: Planks
setup: Forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders, legs straight behind you on your toes.
steps: Lift your hips so your body makes one straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and pull your belly button toward your spine.
Breathe steadily and hold without letting the hips sag or pike up.
mistakes: Looking up and craning the neck

name: Crunches
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat on the floor, fingertips lightly behind your ears.
steps: Breathe out and curl your shoulders up off the floor, chin slightly tucked.
Lift only until your shoulder blades clear the floor. Your lower back stays down.
Pause for a second at the top, then lower slowly.
mistakes: Pulling on your neck with your hands
Lifting the lower back off the floor

name: Leg Raises
setup: Lie flat on your back, legs straight, hands under your hips or flat by your sides.
steps: Keep your legs straight and lift them together until they point at the ceiling.
Lower them slowly until they are just above the floor, without touching down.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor the whole time.
cues: Lower back glued to the floor
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor

name: Bicycle Crunches
setup: Lie on your back, hands lightly behind your ears, knees up at ninety degrees, shins parallel to the floor.
steps: Bring your right elbow toward your left knee while you straighten the right leg out.
Switch sides: left elbow to right knee, left leg straight. That's like pedaling a bike.
Twist from the ribs, not the neck, and keep the pace slow and controlled. One elbow-to-knee each side is one rep.
mistakes: Pulling the head with the hands
Going so fast the abs never work
Letting the straight leg drop to the floor

name: Russian Twists
setup: Sit on the floor, knees bent, lean back a little so your abs switch on. Lift your feet an inch if you can, or keep heels down to make it easier.
steps: Clasp your hands together in front of your chest.
Rotate your torso to the right and tap your hands beside your hip, then rotate to the left and tap.
Keep your chest up and move your shoulders, not just your arms. Right plus left is one rep.

name: Mountain Climbers
muscles: Lower abs, hip flexors, shoulders, plus cardio
setup: Start in a high plank: hands under shoulders, arms straight, body in one line.
steps: Drive your right knee toward your chest, then shoot it back as the left knee comes in.
Keep switching, like running in place with your hands on the floor.
Hips stay level with your shoulders. Don't let them bounce up.

name: Dead Bug
setup: Lie on your back with arms straight up toward the ceiling and knees bent at ninety degrees over your hips.
steps: Breathe out and press your lower back flat into the floor.
Slowly lower your right arm overhead and straighten your left leg toward the floor at the same time.
Come back to the start and switch sides. Left arm, right leg. One each side is one rep.
cues: Lower back flat the whole time

name: Hollow Hold
setup: Lie on your back, arms straight overhead, legs straight and together.
steps: Press your lower back into the floor and lift your shoulders and legs a few inches off the ground.
Your body makes a shallow banana shape. Arms by your ears, toes pointed.
Hold it. If your back lifts, raise the legs higher or bend the knees to make it easier.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor

name: Reverse Crunches
setup: Lie on your back, hands by your sides or under your hips, knees bent and feet off the floor.
steps: Breathe out and pull your knees toward your chest, curling your hips up off the floor.
Lift the hips with your abs, not by swinging the legs.
Lower the hips back down slowly and stop before your feet touch the floor.

name: Side Plank
setup: Lie on your side, forearm on the floor with the elbow under your shoulder, legs stacked.
steps: Lift your hips so your body makes a straight line from head to feet.
Stack your shoulders, hips and feet, and keep your top hand on your hip or reaching up.
Hold, then switch sides for the next set.
mistakes: Shoulder creeping up to the ear

name: Plank Shoulder Taps
setup: Start in a high plank on a mat with your hands under your shoulders, your feet slightly wider than your hips, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Tighten your core and glutes and pull your ribs down toward your hips, so your lower back does not sag.
Lift your right hand and tap your left shoulder, keeping your hips and shoulders as square to the floor as you can.
Set that hand down softly, then tap your right shoulder with your left hand. One tap with each hand is one rep.

name: Plank Jacks
setup: Start in a high plank on a mat with your hands under your shoulders, your feet together, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Tighten your core and pull your ribs toward your hips so your lower back stays flat and your hips stay level.
Jump both feet out wide at the same time, landing softly on the balls of your feet, then jump them back together.
Keep your shoulders over your hands and repeat at a steady pace, slowing down if your hips start to bounce or your back sags.
mistakes: Lower back sagging toward the floor

name: Plank Up-Downs
setup: Start in a high plank on a mat with your hands under your shoulders, your feet hip-width apart, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Tighten your core and glutes and pull your ribs down toward your hips, so your lower back stays flat.
Lower down onto one forearm and then the other, keeping your hips as still as you can, until you are in a forearm plank.
Press back up one hand at a time until your arms are straight. That is one rep. Lead with the other arm next time.

name: Body Saw Planks
setup: Get into a forearm plank on a smooth floor with your elbows under your shoulders and your toes resting on sliders or small towels.
steps: Squeeze your glutes, tighten your core, and pull your ribs down so your body is one straight line from head to heels.
Slowly rock your whole body forward and back a few inches, letting your toes glide on the sliders while your forearms stay planted.
Keep the movement small and smooth, and shorten it if your lower back starts to sag.

name: Reverse Planks
muscles: Abs, glutes, hamstrings, shoulders, lower back
setup: Sit on a mat with your legs straight in front of you and your hands flat on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet.
steps: Press into your hands and heels and lift your hips until your body makes one straight line from shoulders to heels.
Squeeze your glutes so your hips stay high and your lower back does not sag, and keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
Keep your gaze forward, breathe steadily, and hold. Bend your knees and keep your feet flat if you need an easier version.

name: Side Plank Hip Dips
setup: Get into a side plank on a mat, resting on your right forearm with your elbow under your shoulder, your feet stacked, and your hips lifted in a straight line.
steps: Press your forearm into the floor and squeeze your glutes, lifting your hips until your body is one straight line from head to feet.
Slowly lower your bottom hip a few inches toward the floor, keeping your chest facing forward and your ribs pulled in.
Lift your hip back up as high as you can using your side muscles. Finish all your reps, then switch to the other side.
mistakes: Dropping into each dip too fast

name: Hanging Leg Raises
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands just wider than your shoulders, arms straight, and your legs together and straight below you.
steps: Pull your shoulders down away from your ears, tighten your core, and tuck your tailbone slightly under so your lower back does not arch.
Breathe out and lift your straight legs in front of you until they are level with your hips, or higher if you stay controlled.
Pause for a moment, then lower your legs slowly all the way down without swinging, and settle before the next rep.
mistakes: Arching instead of tucking your hips
Dropping your legs at the end

name: Hanging Knee Raises
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands just wider than your shoulders and arms straight, with your legs hanging down together.
steps: Pull your shoulders down away from your ears and tighten your core, so you hang firmly instead of sagging.
Breathe out and lift your knees toward your chest, curling your hips up so your lower back rounds slightly and your ribs move toward your hips.
Lower your legs slowly until you hang straight, with no swinging, and pause before the next rep.

name: Toes-to-Bar
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than your shoulders, arms straight, and your legs together below you.
steps: Pull your shoulders down and grip the bar firmly, then tighten your core and glutes so your body is firm from head to heels.
Breathe out and lift your straight legs, tucking your tailbone under and pulling the bar down toward your thighs, so your lower back rounds instead of arching.
Reach your toes up to touch the bar, or get as close as you can without swinging.
Lower your legs slowly all the way down and settle into a still hang before the next rep.
cues: Pull the bar toward your thighs
mistakes: Loose shoulders and a soft grip

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raises
setup: Step into a captain's chair and rest your forearms on the pads, with your back flat against the backrest, your hands on the handles, and your legs hanging straight down.
steps: Press your back firmly into the backrest, pull your shoulders down, and tighten your core before you move.
Breathe out and bring your knees up toward your chest, curling your pelvis up so your lower back rounds slightly against the pad.
Lower your legs slowly until they hang straight, keeping your back on the pad, and repeat without swinging.
mistakes: Lifting legs without curling your pelvis

name: Cable Crunches
setup: Attach a rope handle to a high pulley on a cable machine, kneel facing the stack, and hold the rope ends beside your ears with your hips over your knees.
steps: Kneel tall with your chest up, hold the rope tight beside your head, and keep your hips still for the whole set.
Breathe out and curl your upper body down, pulling your ribs toward your hips and your elbows toward your thighs.
Squeeze your core at the bottom, then rise back up slowly, keeping the rope beside your head the whole time.
mistakes: Going too heavy to curl properly

name: Ab Wheel Rollouts
setup: Kneel on a mat holding an ab wheel with both hands directly under your shoulders, your back flat and your core tight.
steps: Tuck your tailbone under, pull your ribs down, and squeeze your glutes so your lower back is flat before you move.
Roll the wheel slowly forward, only as far as you can go while keeping your lower back flat and your hips from sagging.
Use your core to pull the wheel back toward your knees, breathing out as you return to the start.
cues: Stop where your back stays flat
mistakes: Lifting your hips to come back

name: Pallof Press
setup: Attach a handle to a cable machine at chest height, stand sideways to the stack with your feet shoulder-width apart, and hold the handle against your chest with both hands.
steps: Step away from the stack until the cable is tight, soften your knees, and stack your ribs over your hips with your core braced.
Press the handle straight out in front of your chest until your arms are straight, resisting the cable's pull to twist you.
Hold for a second with your hips and shoulders square, then bring the handle back in. Finish your reps, then switch sides.

name: Cable Woodchops
setup: Attach a handle to a high pulley on a cable machine, stand sideways to the stack with your feet shoulder-width apart, and hold the handle with both hands above your near shoulder.
steps: Brace your core, keep your ribs down, and soften your knees so your lower back stays in a neutral position.
With your arms almost straight, pull the handle down and across your body toward your opposite knee, turning your chest and hips together.
Control the handle back up along the same path. Finish all your reps on one side, then switch to the other.
mistakes: Twisting only from the lower back

name: Flutter Kicks
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs straight and your hands palms down under your hips.
steps: Press your lower back into the floor, tighten your core, and lift both feet a few inches off the mat.
Kick your legs up and down in small, quick alternating movements, keeping them straight with your toes pointed.
Breathe steadily as you kick. If your lower back starts to lift, raise your legs a little higher or take a short rest.
cues: Lower back stays on the floor
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor

name: Scissor Kicks
muscles: Lower abs, hip flexors, inner thighs
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs straight together and your hands palms down under your hips.
steps: Press your lower back into the floor and tighten your core, then lift both legs about six inches off the mat with your toes pointed.
Open your legs wide, then cross them over each other like scissors, switching which leg is on top each time.
Keep your legs straight and your movements smooth. Raise your legs higher if your lower back starts to lift off the floor.

name: V-Ups
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs straight together and your arms stretched overhead along the floor.
steps: Tighten your core and press your lower back into the floor, with your arms reaching overhead.
Breathe out and lift your straight legs and your chest at the same time, reaching your hands toward your toes to make a V shape.
Pause at the top, then lower back down slowly with control. Bend your knees a little if straight legs are too hard.

name: Sit-Ups
setup: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent, your feet flat on the floor and hip-width apart, and your arms crossed over your chest.
steps: Press your lower back gently into the floor and tighten your core before you move.
Breathe out and curl your upper body up, peeling your spine off the floor one section at a time until you are sitting tall.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower back down slowly one section at a time instead of flopping onto the floor.
cues: Ribs toward hips as you rise

name: Decline Sit-Ups
setup: Lie back on a decline bench with your feet hooked under the pads, your knees bent, and your arms crossed over your chest.
steps: Tighten your core and gently press your lower back into the bench before you move.
Breathe out and curl your upper body up toward your knees, rolling your spine up one section at a time.
Stop when your chest is near your thighs, then lower back down slowly under control, keeping your core tight.

name: Toe Touches
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs pointing straight up toward the ceiling, your feet together, and your arms stretched up toward your toes.
steps: Press your lower back into the floor and tighten your core, keeping your legs still, with a slight bend in your knees if needed.
Breathe out and lift your shoulder blades off the floor, reaching your fingertips up toward your toes.
Pause at the top with your ribs pulled toward your hips, then lower your shoulders back down slowly. Keep your neck relaxed.
mistakes: Craning your neck toward your toes

name: Heel Taps
setup: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent, your feet flat on the floor about a foot from your hips, and your arms by your sides.
steps: Press your lower back into the floor, tighten your core, and lift your shoulder blades just off the mat.
Reach your right hand toward your right heel by bending sideways at your waist, then come back through the middle.
Reach your left hand toward your left heel, keeping your shoulders lifted the whole time. One tap on each side is one rep.
mistakes: Lifting your feet off the floor
Letting your shoulders drop between taps

name: Windshield Wipers
setup: Lie on your back on a mat with your arms out to the sides, palms down, and your legs pointing straight up, or with your knees bent at ninety degrees if that is easier.
steps: Press your arms and shoulders into the floor, flatten your lower back, and tighten your core.
Slowly lower both legs together to the right, only as far as you can keep your shoulders and lower back on the floor.
Use your core to lift your legs back through the middle, then lower them to the left. One to each side is one rep.
cues: Shoulders and lower back stay down
mistakes: Dropping your legs to the floor fast
Going lower than you can control

name: L-Sits
setup: Sit on a mat with your legs straight in front of you and your hands flat on the floor beside your hips, or on parallettes, fingers pointing forward.
steps: Press down through your hands, lock your arms straight, and pull your shoulders down away from your ears.
Squeeze your thighs and tighten your core, then lift your hips and straight legs off the floor with your chest tall and your ribs pulled in.
Hold your legs as level as you can, breathing steadily, then lower gently. If straight legs are too hard, hold with your knees bent.

name: Dragon Flags
setup: Lie on your back on a flat bench, reach overhead, and grip the sides of the bench behind your head with both hands.
steps: Tighten your core and glutes, then curl your knees to your chest and lift your hips until your weight sits on your upper back and shoulders.
Straighten your legs up to the ceiling so your body is one stiff line from shoulders to toes, with your neck relaxed.
Lower your whole body slowly toward the bench as one stiff line, without bending at the hips or arching your lower back, and stop just above it.
Pull your knees back to your chest to reset for the next rep. If a straight body is too hard, keep your knees tucked as you lower.
mistakes: Dropping your body down too fast

name: Suitcase Carry
muscles: Obliques, deep core, grip, upper back
setup: Stand tall holding a heavy dumbbell in one hand at your side, with your feet hip-width apart, your shoulders level, and your free arm relaxed.
steps: Stand tall, tighten your core, and stack your ribs over your hips so you do not lean toward the weight.
Walk forward with short, steady steps, keeping your shoulders level and your body upright as the weight tries to pull you sideways.
Keep a firm grip and steady breathing for the full time, then switch the dumbbell to your other hand and repeat.

name: Bird Dogs
muscles: Deep core, lower back, glutes, shoulders
setup: Get on all fours on a mat with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, keeping a long, flat back and your eyes on the floor.
steps: Tighten your core lightly and keep your ribs pulled in, so your back stays flat like a tabletop.
Slowly reach your right arm forward and your left leg straight back at the same time, until both are in line with your body.
Pause for a second without letting your hips tilt, then lower and switch to your left arm and right leg. One on each side is one rep.

name: Stir the Pot
setup: Place your forearms on a stability ball and walk your feet back into a forearm plank, with your elbows under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
steps: Squeeze your glutes, tighten your core, and pull your ribs down so your lower back stays flat and still.
Using your forearms, draw slow circles on the ball as if stirring a big pot, keeping your hips and shoulders square.
Circle clockwise for half the time, then switch to counterclockwise. Keep the circles small and slow, and make them smaller if your hips wobble.

name: Hollow Rocks
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs straight together and your arms stretched overhead beside your ears.
steps: Press your lower back into the floor, tighten your core, then lift your arms, shoulders, and straight legs off the floor into a shallow banana shape.
Keeping your body stiff, rock gently back and forth like a rocking chair, rolling from your upper back to your lower back.
Keep your lower back pressed down the whole time. If it lifts, raise your legs higher or bend your knees.

name: Tuck-Ups
setup: Sit on a mat with your hands on the floor behind your hips, lean back slightly, and hold your legs straight out a few inches off the floor.
steps: Lift your chest, tighten your core, and keep your spine long so your lower back does not collapse into a deep round.
Breathe out and draw your knees in toward your chest while your upper body leans forward to meet them.
Reach your legs back out as you lean back to the start. Rest your heels lightly on the floor if you need an easier version.
mistakes: Kicking your legs out too hard

name: Standing Oblique Crunches
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, your fingertips lightly behind your ears, and your elbows pointing out to the sides.
steps: Tighten your core and stack your ribs over your hips, then shift your weight onto your left foot.
Lift your right knee out to the side while bending your torso sideways to bring your right elbow down toward it.
Lower your foot, stand tall, and repeat on the left side. One crunch on each side is one rep.

name: Barbell Back Squats
setup: Set a barbell in a squat rack at about chest height, step under it so it rests across your upper back below your neck, grip it outside your shoulders, and stand up to lift it off the hooks.
steps: Step back with your feet shoulder width apart and toes turned slightly out, then breathe deep into your belly and brace your core.
Sit your hips back and down while keeping your chest up and your back flat, and let your knees track out over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, or as deep as you can go while keeping your back flat and your heels down.
Drive up through the middle of your feet, keeping your knees out, and squeeze your glutes as you stand tall.
mistakes: Rounding your lower back at the bottom

name: Leg Press
setup: Sit in the leg press machine with your back and hips flat against the pad, and place your feet shoulder width apart in the middle of the platform.
steps: Press the platform up until your legs are almost straight, release the safety handles, and keep a soft bend in your knees.
Brace your core and lower the platform slowly until your knees are bent to about ninety degrees, keeping your hips and lower back flat on the pad.
Push through your whole foot to press the platform away, stopping just short of locking out your knees.
mistakes: Hips curling up off the pad
Locking your knees at the top

name: Walking Lunges
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your hands on your hips, with a clear stretch of floor about ten steps long in front of you.
steps: Brace your core and stride forward with your right foot, taking a step long enough that your front shin stays close to vertical.
Lower straight down until both knees are bent to about ninety degrees, with your front knee over your ankle and your back knee just above the floor.
Push through your front foot to bring your back leg forward into the next step, alternating legs, and count each step as one rep.
mistakes: Taking steps that are too short
Leaning forward over your front leg

name: Bulgarian Split Squats
setup: Stand about two feet in front of a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, and rest the top of your back foot on the bench behind you.
steps: Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and set your front foot far enough forward that your front shin can stay close to vertical when you lower.
Bend both knees and lower your back knee straight down toward the floor until your front thigh is about parallel, keeping your front knee over your toes.
Press through your whole front foot to stand back up, then finish all your reps on this leg before switching legs.
mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench

name: Leg Extensions
setup: Sit in the leg extension machine with your back against the pad, line your knees up with the machine pivot, and set the ankle pad on your lower shins just above your feet.
steps: Hold the handles at your sides, brace your core, and keep your hips pressed down into the seat.
Straighten your knees to raise the pad until your legs are almost fully straight, then squeeze your thighs for one second.
Lower the pad slowly back to the start without letting the weights rest, keeping your hips down the whole time.

name: Squats
setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out a little, arms out in front.
steps: Push your hips back and bend your knees to sit down, like onto a chair.
Go until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, chest up.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.

name: Front Squats
setup: Set a barbell in a squat rack at about chest height, rest it on the front of your shoulders with your fingertips under the bar and elbows pointing forward, and stand up to lift it off the hooks.
steps: Step back with your feet shoulder width apart and toes turned slightly out, then lift your elbows high so the bar stays pinned on your shoulders.
Breathe deep into your belly, brace your core, then sit straight down between your hips, keeping your chest tall and your knees tracking over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, or as deep as you can go while your elbows stay high and your back stays flat.
Drive up through your whole foot, keeping your elbows high and your torso upright, and squeeze your glutes at the top.

name: Goblet Squats
setup: Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder width and toes turned slightly out, holding one dumbbell upright against your chest with both hands cupped under the top end.
steps: Tuck your elbows in close to your ribs, take a deep breath, and brace your core so your chest stays tall.
Sit your hips back and down, letting your elbows slide just inside your knees, and keep your knees tracking over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor or a little deeper, keeping your heels flat, then press through your whole foot to stand tall.
cues: Brace, then sit between your hips

name: Hack Squats
setup: Step into the hack squat machine with your shoulders under the pads, your back flat against the backrest, and your feet shoulder width apart, a little forward on the platform.
steps: Straighten your legs to lift the sled, release the safety handles, and keep a soft bend in your knees.
Brace your core, then bend your knees to sit down slowly until they reach about ninety degrees, keeping your whole back on the pad.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up, keeping your knees in line with your toes and stopping just short of locking them out.

name: Reverse Lunges
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your hands on your hips, with room behind you to step back.
steps: Brace your core and step straight back with your right foot, landing on the ball of your foot with your heel lifted.
Lower straight down until both knees are bent to about ninety degrees, keeping your front shin close to vertical and your front heel planted.
Push through your front heel to bring your back foot forward to the start, then step back with your left leg, counting each lunge as one rep.
mistakes: Putting weight on your back foot

name: Forward Lunges
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your hands on your hips, with room in front of you to step forward.
steps: Brace your core and take a long step forward with your right foot, landing with your whole foot flat.
Lower straight down until both knees are bent to about ninety degrees, keeping your torso upright and your front knee over your ankle.
Push hard off your front foot to step back to standing, then repeat with your left leg, counting each lunge as one rep.
mistakes: Front heel lifting off the floor

name: Lateral Lunges
setup: Stand tall with your feet together and your hands clasped in front of your chest, with room to step wide to each side.
steps: Brace your core, then take a big step to your right, keeping both toes pointing straight ahead.
Sit your hips back and bend your right knee in line with your toes while your left leg stays straight, keeping both feet flat and your chest up.
Push hard through your right foot to return to the middle, then repeat to the left, counting each lunge as one rep.
cues: Brace, then sit into one hip
mistakes: Heel lifting on the bent leg

name: Step-Ups
setup: Stand facing a sturdy bench or box about knee height with your hands on your hips, or a dumbbell in each hand once the move feels easy.
steps: Brace your core and place your whole right foot on the bench, so your knee is bent to about ninety degrees.
Press through your right heel to stand tall on the bench, bringing your left knee up while keeping your right knee in line with your toes.
Lower your left foot back to the floor slowly, then finish all your reps on this leg before switching sides.
mistakes: Using a bench that is too high

name: Sissy Squats
setup: Stand with your feet hip width apart, hold a sturdy post or squat rack with one hand for balance, and rise onto the balls of your feet.
steps: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body stays in one straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Bend your knees and let them travel forward over your toes as you lean back, lowering slowly only as far as you can control.
Squeeze your thighs to pull yourself back up to standing, keeping your hips pushed forward and your heels off the floor the whole time.
mistakes: Going lower than you can control

name: Wall Sits
setup: Stand with your back against a smooth wall and your feet shoulder width apart, about two feet away from the wall.
steps: Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor and your knees are bent to ninety degrees.
Keep your knees directly over your ankles, press your whole back into the wall, and let your arms hang or fold them across your chest.
Brace your core, breathe steadily, and hold this position until time is up, pushing through your heels.
mistakes: Pushing on your thighs with your hands
Sitting too high up the wall

name: Jump Squats
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and toes turned slightly out, on a flat, non-slip floor with plenty of space around you.
steps: Brace your core, then sit your hips back and bend your knees into a squat, keeping your chest up and your knees tracking over your toes.
Swing your arms back, then explode upward and jump as high as you can, fully straightening your hips and knees.
Land softly on the middle of your feet with your knees bent, sink straight into the next squat, and keep a steady rhythm.
mistakes: Rounding your back in the squat

name: Box Squats
setup: Step under a barbell in a squat rack, rest it across your upper back, walk it out, and stand with your feet slightly wider than your shoulders and a sturdy box or bench about knee height behind you.
steps: Take a big breath, brace your core, and push your hips back first, as if you were reaching your glutes back to the box.
Sit down slowly onto the box with your shins close to vertical, your knees pushed out, and your back flat.
Pause briefly on the box with your core still braced and your chest tall, without relaxing or rocking back.
Drive your feet into the floor, push your knees out, and squeeze your glutes to stand up tall.
cues: Brace, sit back, do not drop
mistakes: Relaxing your core on the box

name: Smith Machine Squats
setup: Set the Smith machine bar at about chest height, step under it so the bar rests across your upper back, and place your feet shoulder width apart, slightly in front of the bar.
steps: Twist your wrists to unhook the bar, take a big breath, and brace your core.
Sit down by bending your knees and hips together, keeping your chest up, your back flat, and your knees tracking over your toes.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, with your heels flat and your weight over the middle of your feet.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall, and twist the bar back onto the hooks when your set is done.
cues: Feet slightly in front of bar

name: Pistol Squats
setup: Stand on one leg beside a sturdy rack or post you can grab for support, with your other leg lifted straight out in front of you and your arms reaching forward.
steps: Brace your core and keep your chest tall, then sit your hips back and bend your standing knee to lower slowly while your other leg stays straight.
Keep your standing heel flat and your knee tracking over your toes as you go down as deep as you can control.
Drive through your whole standing foot to rise back up, then finish all your reps on this leg before switching.
mistakes: Standing heel lifting off the floor

name: Split Squats
setup: Stand in a long split stance with your right foot about two feet in front of your left, both feet pointing forward, and your hands on your hips.
steps: Brace your core, rise onto the ball of your back foot, and keep your torso tall.
Bend both knees and lower straight down until your back knee hovers just above the floor and your front thigh is near parallel.
Press through your whole front foot to rise back up without moving your feet, and finish all your reps before switching legs.
cues: Braced core, straight up and down
mistakes: Front heel lifting off the floor

name: Zercher Squats
setup: Set a barbell in a squat rack at about waist height, squat down to hook the bar in the crooks of your elbows, and clasp your hands together in front of your chest.
steps: Stand up to lift the bar off the hooks, step back, and set your feet shoulder width apart with your toes turned slightly out.
Take a big breath, brace your core, and keep your elbows pointing forward and your chest tall with the bar pulled in tight.
Sit your hips back and down until your thighs are about parallel, keeping your knees tracking over your toes and your back flat.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand tall, keeping the bar close to your body.
mistakes: Bar sliding away from your body

name: Spanish Squats
setup: Anchor a long, heavy resistance band to a sturdy rack or post at knee height, step into the loop so it sits behind your knees, and walk back until the band is tight.
steps: Lean back into the band with your arms reaching forward, keep your chest tall, and brace your core.
Sit your hips down and back until your thighs are about parallel, keeping your shins straight up and down and your heels flat.
Hold this position with your core braced, breathing steadily, until time is up.
cues: Shins stay straight up and down
mistakes: Knees traveling far past your toes
Band anchored too low or loose

name: Cyclist Squats
setup: Stand with your heels raised on small weight plates or a low wedge, your feet close together with toes pointing forward, and your arms reaching out in front.
steps: Brace your core and keep your chest tall, then bend your knees and let them travel forward over your toes as you lower.
Sink as deep as you comfortably can while pressing your heels firmly into the plates and keeping your back flat.
Press through your whole foot to stand back up, keeping your feet close together the whole time.

name: Heel-Elevated Squats
setup: Stand with your heels raised on small weight plates or a low wedge and your feet shoulder width apart, holding one dumbbell upright against your chest with both hands.
steps: Tuck your elbows in, brace your core, and keep your chest tall with your weight spread across your whole foot.
Bend your knees and sit straight down between your hips, letting your knees travel forward over your toes while your heels stay pressed into the plates.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive up through your whole foot to stand tall.

name: Dumbbell Lunges
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your arms straight and your palms facing in.
steps: Pull your shoulders back, brace your core, and take a long step forward with your right foot.
Lower straight down until both knees are bent to about ninety degrees, keeping the dumbbells hanging at your sides and your front knee over your ankle.
Push through your front foot to step back to standing, then repeat with your left leg, counting each lunge as one rep.

name: Romanian Deadlifts
setup: Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip just outside your hips, your feet hip width apart, and a soft bend in your knees.
steps: Take a deep breath, brace your core, and pull your shoulder blades back and down so your back stays flat.
Push your hips straight back, keeping your knees softly bent, and slide the bar down your thighs as you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Stop when the bar reaches about mid-shin, or just before your lower back would start to round, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand tall, without leaning back at the top.
mistakes: Bending your knees into a squat

name: Lying Leg Curls
setup: Lie face down on the leg curl machine with your knees just off the end of the pad, in line with the pivot, and the roller resting on the backs of your lower legs just above your heels.
steps: Grip the handles and press your hips down into the pad so they stay glued there for the whole set.
Bend your knees to curl your heels toward your glutes as far as you can, then squeeze your hamstrings for one second.
Lower the roller slowly until your legs are almost straight, keeping control of the weight the entire time.

name: Seated Leg Curls
setup: Sit in the seated leg curl machine with your back against the pad, your legs straight, the roller just above your heels, and the thigh pad snug across the top of your thighs.
steps: Hold the handles, sit tall with your back against the pad, and brace your core.
Bend your knees to pull the roller down and back as far as you can, then squeeze your hamstrings for one second.
Let the roller rise slowly until your legs are almost straight, keeping your hips pressed back into the seat.
mistakes: Lifting your hips off the seat

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlifts
setup: Stand on your right leg with a soft bend in the knee, holding one dumbbell in your left hand in front of your thigh, with your left foot just off the floor.
steps: Brace your core, then hinge forward from your hips, sliding the dumbbell down your leg as your free leg lifts straight back behind you.
Lower until your torso and free leg form one long line near parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat and your hips level.
Squeeze your glute and drive your hips forward to stand tall, then finish all your reps on this leg before switching.
cues: Long line from head to heel

name: Glute-Ham Raises
setup: Set up the glute-ham raise machine so your ankles are locked under the pads, your feet are flat on the footplate, and the front pad supports the tops of your thighs.
steps: Cross your arms over your chest, brace your core, and lower your body forward and down with your back flat until your torso hangs toward the floor.
Squeeze your hamstrings and glutes to lift your body back up, keeping your back flat and your core braced, until your body is in a straight line.
Lower back down slowly under control, without bouncing at the bottom, and repeat.
mistakes: Arching your lower back at the top

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlifts
setup: Stand with your feet hip width apart and a soft bend in your knees, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with your palms facing you.
steps: Take a deep breath, brace your core, and pull your shoulders back and down so your back stays flat.
Push your hips straight back and let the dumbbells slide down the front of your legs, keeping your knees softly bent.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, around mid-shin, stopping before your lower back would round.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand tall, keeping the dumbbells close to your legs.

name: Stiff-Leg Deadlifts
setup: Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip just outside your hips, your feet hip width apart, and your legs almost straight with only a tiny bend in your knees.
steps: Take a deep breath, brace your core, and lock in a flat back with your shoulders pulled back and down.
Keeping your legs almost straight, fold forward from your hips and slide the bar down your thighs with your back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the back of your thighs, usually around mid-shin, before your lower back starts to round.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand tall, keeping the bar close to your legs.
cues: Legs nearly straight, fold at hips
mistakes: Rounding your back to reach lower

name: Standing Leg Curls
setup: Stand facing the standing leg curl machine, hold the handles, and rest the back of one lower leg, just above the heel, against the roller pad.
steps: Stand tall on your other leg with a soft bend in the knee, brace your core, and keep your hips square to the machine.
Bend your working knee to curl your heel toward your glute as far as you can without letting your thigh swing back, then squeeze for a second.
Lower the roller slowly back to the start, and finish all your reps on this leg before switching legs.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curls
setup: Kneel on a soft mat with your ankles anchored under a sturdy bar or held down by a partner, and your body upright in a straight line from knees to head.
steps: Cross your arms in front of your chest, brace your core, and squeeze your glutes so your body stays in one straight line.
Lean forward from your knees as slowly as you can, keeping your body in one straight line and resisting the fall with your hamstrings.
When you cannot hold on, catch yourself with your hands, then push off the floor just enough to return to the start.

name: Good Mornings
setup: Set a barbell across your upper back in a squat rack as for a back squat, then walk it out with your feet hip width apart and a soft bend in your knees.
steps: Take a deep breath, brace your core, and squeeze your shoulder blades together to hold the bar tight against your back.
Push your hips straight back and let your chest tip forward, keeping your back flat and your knees softly bent.
Lower until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, or until you feel a deep hamstring stretch, but stop before your back rounds.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to bring your torso back upright.

name: Stability Ball Hamstring Curls
setup: Lie on your back on a mat with your heels on top of a stability ball, your legs straight, and your arms flat at your sides.
steps: Press your heels into the ball and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your ankles.
Keeping your hips high, bend your knees and roll the ball toward your glutes until the soles of your feet are flat on it.
Slowly straighten your legs to roll the ball back out, keeping your hips lifted the entire time.
cues: Hips stay high all the way

name: Slider Leg Curls
setup: Lie on your back on a smooth floor with your heels on sliders or small towels, your knees bent, and your arms flat at your sides.
steps: Press through your heels to lift your hips into a bridge, with your body in a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Keep your hips high and slowly slide your heels away from you until your legs are almost straight.
Pull your heels back toward your glutes by curling your hamstrings, keeping your hips lifted the whole time.
mistakes: Hips sagging as you slide out
Sliding out faster than you control

name: Sumo Deadlifts
setup: Stand with your feet wide and toes turned out, with a loaded barbell on the floor over the middle of your feet, close to your shins.
steps: Sit your hips down and back, bend forward, and grip the bar with straight arms and your hands inside your knees.
Take a big breath, brace your core, lift your chest so your back is flat, and push your knees out over your toes.
Push the floor apart with your feet and stand up, keeping the bar close to your legs and your chest up.
Finish by squeezing your glutes at the top, then lower the bar back down along your legs with a flat back.
mistakes: Hips shooting up before the bar
Bar drifting away from your legs

name: Cable Pull-Throughs
setup: Attach a rope to the low pulley of a cable machine, stand facing away from it, straddle the cable, and hold the rope in both hands between your legs.
steps: Walk a few steps forward until the weight lifts, set your feet shoulder width apart, and soften your knees.
Brace your core and push your hips straight back, letting your hands reach back between your legs while your back stays flat.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand tall, keeping your arms straight like hooks.

name: Hip Thrusts
setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the edge of a sturdy bench, roll a padded barbell over your hips, and plant your feet flat about hip width apart.
steps: Lean back so the bench sits just under your shoulder blades, then tuck your chin and brace your core with the bar resting over your hips.
Drive through your heels and push your hips up until your shins are vertical and your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top for a second, keeping your ribs down so your lower back does not arch.
Lower your hips slowly until they are just above the floor, then press up again.
mistakes: Arching your lower back at the top
Feet placed too far from your hips

name: Cable Kickbacks
setup: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable pulley, fasten it around one ankle, face the machine, and hold the frame with both hands, standing slightly back from it.
steps: Lean forward slightly from your hips with a flat back, brace your core, and keep your standing knee softly bent.
Kick your working leg straight back and slightly up until you feel your glute squeeze, without arching your lower back.
Return slowly to the start without letting the weights rest, and finish all your reps on this leg before switching.
cues: Squeeze your glute at the top

name: Sumo Squats
setup: Stand with your feet much wider than your shoulders and toes turned out about forty-five degrees, holding one dumbbell hanging down between your legs with both hands.
steps: Take a deep breath, brace your core, and keep your chest tall with the dumbbell hanging between your legs.
Bend your knees and lower straight down between your hips, pushing your knees out over your toes, until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Press through your whole foot and squeeze your glutes and inner thighs to stand back up tall.

name: Curtsy Lunges
muscles: Glutes, quads, inner and outer thighs
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your hands clasped in front of your chest.
steps: Brace your core, shift your weight onto your left leg, then step your right foot back and across behind your left leg, like a curtsy.
Bend both knees and lower until your front thigh is near parallel, keeping your chest tall and your front knee tracking over your toes.
Push through your front heel to stand and bring your back foot to the start, then switch sides, counting each lunge as one rep.

name: Banded Lateral Walks
setup: Place a looped resistance band around your thighs just above your knees and stand with your feet hip width apart, in a slight squat with your knees softly bent.
steps: Sit your hips back into a quarter squat, brace your core, and keep your chest tall and your toes pointing forward.
Step to the side with your lead foot, pushing that knee out against the band, then bring your other foot in without letting your feet touch.
Take half your steps in one direction, then walk back the other way, counting every step as one rep.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrusts
setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the edge of a sturdy bench, one foot flat on the floor, and your other knee pulled in toward your chest.
steps: Lean back so the bench sits just under your shoulder blades, then tuck your chin and brace your core.
Drive through the heel of your planted foot to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knee to shoulders.
Squeeze your glute at the top, keeping your hips level, then lower slowly and finish all your reps on this leg before switching.

name: Barbell Glute Bridges
setup: Sit on the floor with a padded barbell over your thighs, lie back with your knees bent and feet flat, and roll the bar to your hips, holding it with both hands.
steps: Set your feet flat about hip width apart, close enough that your shins will be vertical at the top, and brace your core.
Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without arching your lower back, then lower your hips slowly to the floor.
mistakes: Feet too far from your hips
Letting the bar roll toward your stomach

name: Glute Bridges
setup: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent, your feet flat and hip width apart, and your arms resting at your sides.
steps: Brace your core, then press through your heels to lift your hips off the floor.
Keep lifting until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders, and squeeze your glutes at the top.
Hold for a second, then lower your hips slowly back to the floor.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridges
setup: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, then lift one leg and straighten it so it lines up with your other thigh.
steps: Brace your core and keep your hips level, with the lifted leg held straight and in line with your other thigh.
Push through the heel of your planted foot to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knee to shoulders.
Squeeze your glute at the top, lower slowly, and finish all your reps on this leg before switching.

name: Banded Glute Bridges
setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat about hip width apart, and a looped resistance band around your thighs just above your knees.
steps: Press your knees out against the band so you feel your outer hips working, and brace your core.
Push through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders, keeping your knees pressing out.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly while keeping tension on the band.
cues: Knees press out on the band

name: Standing Glute Kickbacks
setup: Stand facing a wall or sturdy chair with both hands on it for balance, your feet hip width apart, and your weight on one leg.
steps: Brace your core, keep your hips square to the wall, and keep a soft bend in your standing knee.
Kick your other leg straight back and slightly up, squeezing your glute at the top, without arching your lower back.
Lower your leg slowly without touching the floor, and finish all your reps on this leg before switching.
cues: Squeeze your glute at the top

name: Donkey Kicks
setup: Get on your hands and knees on a mat with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
steps: Brace your core and keep your back flat and your neck long.
Keeping your right knee bent to ninety degrees, lift that leg until your thigh is in line with your back and your foot points at the ceiling.
Squeeze your glute at the top, lower your knee back to the start, and finish all your reps on this leg before switching.

name: Fire Hydrants
setup: Get on your hands and knees on a mat with your hands under your shoulders, your knees under your hips, and your back flat.
steps: Brace your core and keep your hips level and square to the floor.
Keeping your right knee bent at ninety degrees, lift that knee out to the side until your thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Lower slowly without rocking your torso, and finish all your reps on this leg before switching.
mistakes: Leaning away from the lifting leg
Letting your back arch or sag

name: Frog Pumps
setup: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet pressed together, your knees dropped open to the sides, and your heels close to your glutes.
steps: Rest your arms at your sides and brace your core so your ribs stay down.
Press through the outer edges of your feet and lift your hips straight up, squeezing your glutes hard at the top.
Lower your hips slowly to just above the floor, then pump up again at a steady pace.
cues: Squeeze glutes hard at the top
mistakes: Using your lower back to lift

name: Hip Abduction Machine
setup: Sit in the hip abduction machine with your back against the pad, your feet on the footrests, and the leg pads resting against the outsides of your thighs.
steps: Sit tall, brace your core, and hold the handles at your sides.
Push your legs apart as wide as you comfortably can, leading with your knees, and squeeze your outer glutes for a second.
Bring your legs back slowly until the pads are almost touching, without letting the weights rest.
cues: Sit tall, back on the pad

name: Banded Clamshells
setup: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, your head resting on your lower arm, and a looped resistance band around your thighs just above your knees.
steps: Stack your hips directly on top of each other, keep your feet together, and lightly brace your core.
Keeping your feet touching, lift your top knee toward the ceiling as far as you can without rolling your hips backward.
Pause for a moment, lower your knee slowly, and finish all your reps on this side before switching.

name: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlifts
setup: Stand with your feet wide and toes turned out, with a kettlebell on the floor between your feet, in line with your ankles.
steps: Sit your hips back and down, reach for the handle with both hands, and keep your arms straight.
Breathe in, brace your core, flatten your back by lifting your chest, and press your knees out in line with your toes.
Push the floor away with your feet and stand tall, keeping the kettlebell close to your body, then squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower the kettlebell the same way, sitting your hips back with a flat back, until it touches the floor.

name: Standing Calf Raises
setup: Stand in a standing calf raise machine with your shoulders under the pads and the balls of your feet on the platform, with your heels hanging off the edge.
steps: Stand tall with your knees straight but not locked, lift the pads off their stops, and brace your core.
Lower your heels slowly until you feel a deep stretch in your calves.
Press through the balls of your feet to rise as high as you can, pause for one second, then lower with control.

name: Seated Calf Raises
setup: Sit in the seated calf raise machine with the pad snug across your lower thighs, the balls of your feet on the platform, and your knees bent to about ninety degrees.
steps: Sit tall, lift the pad slightly, release the safety bar, and brace your core.
Lower your heels slowly, letting your knees rise a little, until you feel a deep stretch in your calves.
Push through the balls of your feet to lift the weight as high as you can, pause for one second, then lower with control.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raises
setup: Stand on the edge of a sturdy step on the ball of one foot, lift your other foot off the step, and rest your fingertips on a wall or rail for balance.
steps: Keep your standing knee straight but not locked, brace your core, and stand tall.
Lower your heel below the step until you feel a deep stretch in your calf.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes, pause for a second, then lower slowly, and finish all your reps before switching legs.
cues: Stay balanced over your big toe
mistakes: Rolling onto the outside of your foot
Leaning on the wall for support

name: Donkey Calf Raises
setup: Stand on the platform of a donkey calf raise machine with the balls of your feet on the edge, bend forward at your hips, and settle the pad snugly across your lower back.
steps: Hold the handles, keep your back flat and your knees straight but not locked, and lower your heels until you feel a deep stretch.
Press through the balls of your feet to rise as high as you can, squeezing your calves.
Pause for one second at the top, then lower slowly back into the stretch.

name: Leg Press Calf Raises
setup: Sit in the leg press machine with your back flat on the pad and your legs straight, and place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform with your heels hanging off.
steps: Press the platform up until your legs are straight but not locked, release the safety handles, and keep your knees still for the whole set.
Let the platform pull your toes back slowly until you feel a deep stretch in your calves.
Push through the balls of your feet to point your toes as far as you can, pause for one second, then return slowly.

name: Tibialis Raises
muscles: Shins, front of the lower legs
setup: Stand with your back and hips against a wall and your heels about a foot away from it, with your feet hip width apart and your legs straight.
steps: Brace your core, keep your legs straight, and keep your hips against the wall.
Lift the front of your feet toward your shins as high as you can, keeping your heels on the floor.
Pause for a moment at the top, then lower your toes slowly back to the floor.

name: Smith Machine Calf Raises
setup: Place a low step or weight plate under a Smith machine bar, step under the bar so it rests across your upper back, and set the balls of your feet on the edge of the step.
steps: Twist the bar to unhook it, stand tall with your knees straight but not locked, and brace your core.
Lower your heels slowly below the step until you feel a deep stretch in your calves.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes, pause for a second, lower with control, and twist the bar back onto the hooks when you finish.

name: Burpees
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on a clear patch of floor, with your arms by your sides and your weight over your whole foot.
steps: Push your hips back, bend your knees, and place your hands flat on the floor in front of your feet.
Jump or step your feet back into a high plank, lower your chest to the floor, and press up with your core tight.
Hop your feet back to your hands, then stand and jump straight up, landing softly with bent knees. Keep a steady rhythm you can hold.

name: Jump Rope
setup: Stand tall with a jump rope handle in each hand, the rope resting behind your heels, and your elbows tucked close to your sides.
steps: Swing the rope over your head with small circles of your wrists, keeping your hands out at hip height and your elbows close to your sides.
As the rope comes down, jump just high enough to clear it, about one inch off the floor, and land softly on the balls of your feet.
Stay tall with soft knees and a lightly tight core, and find an easy, steady rhythm you could hold for the full time.
mistakes: Swinging the rope with big arms

name: Kettlebell Swings
muscles: Glutes, hamstrings, lower back, shoulders, core
setup: Stand with your feet slightly wider than your shoulders and your toes turned out a little, with a kettlebell on the floor about a foot in front of you.
steps: Push your hips back with your feet flat on the floor, keeping your back straight and your chest proud, and grip the handle with both hands.
Hike the bell back between your legs, high up on your thighs, like you are passing a football behind you.
Snap your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to float the bell up to chest height, keeping your arms relaxed and standing tall at the top.
Let the bell fall back down, hinge your hips back to guide it between your legs, and repeat at a steady rhythm, stopping if your form slips.
mistakes: Lifting the bell with your arms
Rounding your lower back at the bottom

name: High Knees
setup: Stand tall on a clear patch of floor with your feet hip-width apart and your arms bent at ninety degrees in front of you.
steps: Drive your right knee up toward hip height while your left arm swings forward, then quickly switch legs as if you are running on the spot.
Stay on the balls of your feet and land softly under your hips, with your chest tall and your core lightly tight.
Start at a quick but controlled pace, and speed up only if you can keep your knees high and your landings quiet.
mistakes: Going so fast your knees drop

name: Battle Ropes
muscles: Shoulders, arms, upper back, core, legs
setup: Stand facing the anchor point of a battle rope, holding one end in each hand, with your feet shoulder-width apart, your knees bent, and a little slack in the rope.
steps: Sit your hips back into a quarter squat, keep your chest up and your back flat, and tighten your core.
Raise one hand and then the other in quick, alternating movements, whipping the rope into waves that travel all the way to the anchor.
Keep your feet planted and your knees soft, and breathe steadily. Set a pace you can hold for the full time and push harder near the end.
mistakes: Using only your arms for waves

name: Jumping Jacks
setup: Stand tall on a clear patch of floor with your feet together and your arms by your sides.
steps: Jump your feet out wide while you sweep your arms up overhead, landing softly on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent.
Jump your feet back together as your arms come back down to your sides.
Keep your chest tall and find a steady rhythm you can hold for the full time, slowing down if your landings get loud.
mistakes: Rushing until your form falls apart

name: Butt Kicks
setup: Stand tall on a clear patch of floor with your feet hip-width apart and your arms bent at ninety degrees at your sides.
steps: Jog on the spot and flick your right heel up toward your glutes, then your left, keeping your thighs pointing mostly down.
Land softly on the balls of your feet right under your hips, with your chest tall and your core lightly tight.
Pump your arms with each step and keep a quick, springy rhythm you can hold for the full time, easing off if you tire.

name: Skater Jumps
setup: Stand tall on a clear patch of floor with your feet hip-width apart, your knees slightly bent, and your arms relaxed in front of you.
