steps: Push off your right foot and bound sideways to the left, landing softly on your left foot with your knee bent over your toes.
Let your right leg swing behind you without touching down, with your chest leaning slightly forward and your arms swinging across your body for balance.
Now push off your left foot and bound back to the right. Start with small, controlled bounds and only stretch wider when your landings feel steady.

name: Dumbbell Thrusters
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing each other and your elbows pointing forward.
steps: Tighten your core, keep your ribs down and chest tall, and sit your hips back and down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive up through your heels and, as you stand, press the dumbbells overhead in one smooth motion until your arms are straight.
Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders as you sink into your next squat, keeping a steady rhythm you can hold for every rep.

name: Rowing Machine
setup: Sit on a rowing machine with your feet strapped in across the balls of your feet, your knees bent, your arms straight, and the handle held in both hands.
steps: Push through your feet to straighten your legs first, keeping your arms straight and your back tall and flat.
Once your legs are straight, lean back slightly from your hips and pull the handle to your lower ribs with your elbows close.
Return in the reverse order: straighten your arms, lean forward from your hips, then bend your knees to slide the seat forward.
Move at a steady pace you could keep up for the whole time, taking about twice as long to return as to push.

name: Sled Push
setup: Stand behind a weighted sled on turf or a gym floor with good grip, with your hands on the high handles, your arms straight, and your body leaning forward in one straight line.
steps: Brace your core, keep your back flat, and drive one foot into the floor to start the sled moving.
Take short, powerful steps, pushing through the balls of your feet, with your arms straight and your hips low.
Keep your chest up and set a steady pace you can hold for the full time, easing off if your back starts to round.
cues: Drive your feet through the floor

name: Box Jumps
setup: Stand facing a sturdy, stable box at a height you can clear comfortably, with your feet hip-width apart and a short step back from it.
steps: Bend your knees into a quarter squat with your hips back and chest up, and swing your arms back behind you.
Swing your arms forward and jump up onto the box, landing softly on both feet at once with your knees bent.
Stand tall on the box, step down one foot at a time, and take a breath before the next jump so every rep stays crisp.
mistakes: Jumping off instead of stepping down
Choosing a box that is too tall

name: Running
setup: Stand tall on flat ground or a treadmill in supportive running shoes, with your arms bent at ninety degrees and your shoulders relaxed.
steps: Begin with an easy jog, leaning slightly forward from your ankles, with your head up and your eyes looking ahead.
Take quick, light steps and land softly with your foot under your body, not reaching out in front of you.
Swing your arms from front to back, keep your shoulders relaxed, and run at a pace where you could still talk in short sentences.
mistakes: Reaching your foot out in front

name: Stair Climber
setup: Step onto the stair climber and stand tall with your whole foot flat on each step, resting your fingertips lightly on the side rails.
steps: Start the machine at an easy speed and stand tall with your chest up and your hips under your shoulders.
Step up in a smooth rhythm, pressing through your whole foot on every step with your heel staying down, rather than climbing on your toes.
Rest your fingertips lightly on the rails for balance instead of leaning on them, and pick a speed you could keep going for the full time.

name: Bear Crawls
setup: Start on all fours on a clear patch of floor with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, then lift your knees about two inches off the floor.
steps: Keep your back flat and your core tight, with your hips low and level and your knees hovering just off the floor.
Move your right hand and left foot forward together by a few inches, then your left hand and right foot, taking small steps.
Step lightly on your palms and the balls of your feet, and crawl at a slow, steady pace, forward or backward if you run out of space.

name: Man Makers
muscles: Chest, back, shoulders, thighs, glutes, core
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on a clear patch of floor, holding a hex dumbbell in each hand so the weights will not roll when you set them down.
steps: Lower the dumbbells to the floor under your shoulders, then jump or step your feet back into a wide plank with your core tight.
Do one push-up, then row the right dumbbell to your ribs and lower it, then row the left, keeping your hips square to the floor.
Jump or step your feet forward to the dumbbells, landing softly, then stand up, pulling the weights to your shoulders in one smooth motion.
Press both dumbbells overhead with your ribs down until your arms are straight, then lower them to the floor. Rest as needed between reps.
mistakes: Rolling your hips open on rows
Using weights that are too heavy

name: Turkish Get-Ups
setup: Lie on your back with a kettlebell pressed straight up in your right hand, your right knee bent with the foot flat, and your left arm and leg out at forty-five degrees.
steps: Brace your core and keep your eyes on the bell and your arm vertical, then roll onto your left elbow and press up onto your left hand.
Push through your right foot, squeeze your glutes, and lift your hips high, then sweep your left leg back and set that knee down behind you.
Lift your left hand off the floor and your chest tall, keeping the bell locked overhead, then drive through your front foot to stand up.
Reverse each step slowly, pausing in each position, until you are lying down. That is one rep; switch the bell to the other hand for the next.
mistakes: Starting with a bell too heavy
Letting the bell arm drift forward

name: Sprawls
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on a clear patch of floor, with your knees slightly bent and your arms by your sides.
steps: Push your hips back, bend your knees, and drop your hands to the floor in front of you, shoulder-width apart.
Kick both feet back at once, landing on the balls of your feet with your legs long and your hips low but not touching the floor.
Snap your feet back in under your hips and stand up tall. Keep a quick, steady rhythm you can hold for every rep.

name: Medicine Ball Slams
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on a flat floor with clear space around you, holding a slam ball in both hands at your chest.
steps: Raise the ball overhead with your arms long, rising onto your toes and standing tall, with your ribs pulled down so you do not lean back.
Slam the ball into the floor in front of your feet as hard as you can, bending at your hips and knees and using your whole body.
Squat down with a flat back to pick the ball up with both hands, then stand and raise it overhead again. Keep a steady, powerful pace.
mistakes: Rounding your back to pick up

name: Broad Jumps
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart on a flat, non-slip surface with plenty of clear space ahead of you.
steps: Swing your arms back and bend your knees into a quarter squat, with your hips back, your back flat, and your chest up.
Swing your arms forward hard and jump forward as far as you can, pushing off with your whole foot.
Land softly on both feet with your knees bent and your hips back. Hold the landing for a second, then walk back and reset.
mistakes: Leaning too far forward on landing
Jumping again before you are steady

name: Shadow Boxing
setup: Stand with your feet a little wider than your shoulders, your left foot a step ahead of your right, knees soft, and your fists up beside your chin, or swap feet if you are left-handed.
steps: Stay light on the balls of your feet with your chin tucked, your elbows close to your ribs, and your knees soft.
Throw a straight punch with your lead hand, then your back hand, turning your back foot and hips and snapping each hand back to your chin.
Breathe out with every punch and keep moving your feet, starting relaxed and speeding up only as long as your form stays sharp.
mistakes: Crossing your feet when you move

name: Cycling
setup: Set the seat of a stationary bike so your knee has a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke, then sit with the balls of your feet on the pedals.
steps: Sit tall with your hands resting lightly on the handlebars, your shoulders relaxed, and your core lightly tight.
Press down through the balls of your feet and pedal in smooth circles, keeping your knees tracking straight over your toes.
Ease into the first few turns, then pick a resistance and speed where you could still talk in short sentences.

name: Inchworms
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart on a mat and your arms by your sides, ready to fold forward.
steps: Hinge forward at your hips and place your hands flat on the floor in front of your feet, bending your knees as much as you need.
Walk your hands forward slowly, a little at a time, until you are in a high plank with your core tight and your ribs pulled in.
Take tiny steps with your feet toward your hands, keeping your legs fairly straight, then stand tall. That is one rep.

name: Tuck Jumps
muscles: Thighs, glutes, calves, hip flexors, core
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart on a flat, non-slip surface with plenty of clear space above and around you.
steps: Bend your knees into a quarter squat, swing your arms back, then jump straight up, driving your arms forward and up.
At the top, pull your knees up toward your chest, keeping your chest tall rather than folding forward.
Land softly on both feet with your knees bent and your hips back, then pause and reset before the next jump.
mistakes: Folding forward to meet your knees
Pushing on once landings get loud

name: Dumbbell Clean and Press
muscles: Glutes, hamstrings, upper back, shoulders, triceps
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with your palms facing you.
steps: Hinge your hips back with a flat back and soft knees, and lower the dumbbells to just above your knees.
Drive through your whole foot and snap your hips forward to stand tall, shrugging as you pull the dumbbells up close to your body.
Rotate your elbows forward to catch the dumbbells on your shoulders with soft knees, then press them overhead, ribs down, until your arms are straight.
Lower the weights back to your shoulders, then down to your thighs with control, and reset before the next rep.
cues: Ribs over hips as you press
mistakes: Curling the weights with your arms
Rounding your back at the bottom

name: Squat Thrusts
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on a clear patch of floor with your arms by your sides.
steps: Bend your knees, push your hips back, and place your hands flat on the floor in front of you, shoulder-width apart.
Jump both feet back at once into a high plank, landing on the balls of your feet with your core tight and your back flat.
Jump your feet back in beside your hands, then stand up tall with no push-up and no jump at the top. That is one rep.
mistakes: Hips piking up in the air
Hands set too far in front

name: Lateral Shuffles
setup: Stand in an athletic stance with your feet a little wider than your shoulders, your knees bent, your hips back, your chest up, and your hands in front of you.
steps: Push off your trailing foot and slide sideways, taking small quick steps and keeping your feet from crossing or clicking together.
Stay low with your hips back and your chest tall, and keep your weight on the balls of your feet so your landings stay quiet.
After a few steps, plant your lead foot and push off it to shuffle back the other way. Keep a quick rhythm you can hold.
mistakes: Standing up tall as you move
